LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin predict this weekend's top games Getty Images Last week in the NFL was full of drama. The Cleveland Browns came back from down 17-0 to defeat the Houston Texans , while Kirk Cousins was victorious in his first game back with the Minnesota Vikings . The San Francisco 49ers and Dallas Cowboys put up 86 total points in Arlington, and the Cincinnati Bengals blew out Aaron Rodgers and the Pittsburgh Steelers on "Sunday Night Football." This week there's more. Fernando Mendoza will make the first road start of his career against an aggressive Denver Broncos defense, the Detroit Lions will begin life without Aidan Hutchinson at home against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , and the Vikings will play the 49ers in Mexico City in what could go down as one of the best primetime matchups of the entire season. There are many, many massive spreads in the NFL this week! Which teams should you pick in Week 11, and which should you fade? CBS Sports writers Jordan Dajani and Jared Dubin are here to break down the biggest games of the weekend. For clarity, lines for these selections were taken on Nov. 18 over at DraftKings Sportsbook. Indianapolis Colts at Houston Texans (-12.5) (TNF) Dajani (Texans -12.5): I would typically lean toward a huge underdog like this in a divisional game, but two factors have me leaning the other way. One, Daniel Jones threw for just 108 yards, one touchdown and two interceptions last week against the Miami Dolphins . They were starting a quarterback that had never played in the NFL, yet only lost by two points. Jones has been terrible. He's turned the ball over an NFL-high 15 times and has the worst record in primetime by any quarterback since 1970 at 1-16. Additionally, the Texans allowed the Browns to come back from down 17-0 and win their meeting last week, which I imagine has this Texans team seeing red. C.J. Stroud and Co. are better than their 3-6 record indicates. They even beat the Jacksonville Jaguars earlier this season. I think the large number is justified. … Prediction: Texans 27, Colts 14 Dubin (Colts +12.5): I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. … Prediction: Texans 23, Colts 13 Tampa Bay Buccaneers at Detroit Lions (-7) Dajani (Buccaneers +7): Jahmyr Gibbs leads the NFL in rushing yards this season with 1,000, while the Buccaneers allow the fewest rushing yards per game (79.2). The Bucs also lead the NFL in rushing offense and in takeaways with 21. With the Buccaneers coming off their bye week and the Lions coming off an international trip that cost them Aidan Hutchinson for the season, I'm leaning toward Tampa Bay with the points. The Bucs are 4-1 against the spread in their last five games, but keep an eye on the quarterback situation over the next 24 hours. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 21 Dubin (Lions -7): The Bucs likely playing this game without Baker Mayfield pushed me in this direction. Jalon Daniels is fine, but I don't expect the passing game to be able to do much here. The Bucs base the entire offense around the run anyway, but the Lions are actually pretty tough to run on. That could change without Aidan Hutchinson, obviously, but I don't think it will change enough for Tampa's offense to keep pace with what the Lions are likely to do. … Prediction: Lions 24, Buccaneers 16 Las Vegas Raiders at Denver Broncos (-10) Dajani (Broncos -10): I don't think Fernando Mendoza wins his second career start in an environment like Mile High, but can he cover the double-digit spread? Denver has won just one game by double digits this season, back in Week 7 against the Arizona Cardinals . The Las Vegas Raiders, on the other hand, have covered in four straight divisional games for the first time since 2022. The Broncos are coming off their bye week and have scored at least 26 points in each of their last three games. Bo Nix has also thrown multiple touchdowns in back-to-back games. The Raiders are tied for the worst scoring defense in the NFL this year with 28.9 points allowed per game, so I think the Broncos could reach 30 points this week. That could make it tough for Mendoza to cover the spread. He's actually the first rookie quarterback to ever face both of the previous season's No. 1 seeds in his first two career starts. … Prediction: Broncos 30, Raiders 17 Dubin (Raiders +10): The Broncos have seven wins this year, and six of them are by one score. The only team they beat by more than seven points is the Cardinals. I reserve the right to change this pick if Brock Bowers is out and Fernando Mendoza just doesn't have anyone at all to throw the ball to, but otherwise the Broncos just don't seem like a team capable of blowing out an opponent that has actually played fairly well this year. … Prediction: Broncos 21, Raiders 17 Jacksonville Jaguars (-6) at New York Giants Dajani ( Giants +6): No one is debating that the Jaguars are not one of the best teams in the NFL, but they haven't exactly been tested recently. They blew out the hapless Colts, had no problem with Joe Fagnano 's Baltimore Ravens and then dropped 40 points on the one-win Tennessee Titans . The Giants aren't Super Bowl contenders, but this is easily the best team Jacksonville has played in over the past month. I'm not going to take the Giants to win this game straight up, but I am leaning toward the six points. The Giants have an underrated defense that currently ranks No. 5 in the NFL in yards allowed per game (305.7), and J.J. McCarthy has the fifth-most yards per attempt (8.8) since his Giants debut in Week 5. Both of these teams are 6-3 ATS this season. Give me the Giants with a back-door cover. … Prediction: Jaguars 23, Giants 18 Dubin (Jaguars -6): Unlike the Broncos, the Jaguars have blown out everybody. Five of their seven wins have come by 17 points or more, including each of their last three games. The Giants are probably better than the Colts, Ravens and Titans, but I don't see them hanging with this Jacksonville offense — not with the Jags getting their new defensive stalwarts on the field for the first time since the trade deadline. ( Jessie Bates III and Jordan Davis sat out last week because they had yet to have their bye and the Jags had already taken theirs.) … Prediction: Jaguars 31, Giants 20 Minnesota Vikings vs. San Francisco 49ers (-3) (SNF in Mexico City) Dajani (49ers -3): The 49ers are coming off a ridiculous 46-40 win over the Cowboys, where they recorded the most total yards in a road game in franchise history (584) and averaged a whopping 9.4 yards per play. Brock Purdy's offense had three touchdowns of 65+ yards! Christian McCaffrey actually became the first running back in NFL history to record two 65-yard receiving touchdowns in a game. Obviously, the Vikings' defense is MUCH better than the Cowboys', but something you should know is that this game is in Mexico City. And both teams have prepared for it differently . The stadium the 49ers and Vikings will play in on Sunday is over 7,000 feet above sea level. So, the 49ers traveled to the U.S. Air Force Academy in Colorado Springs this week, which is at an elevation of 6,621 feet , to prepare. The Vikings, on the other hand, apparently built an altitude chamber so players can get familiar with "thinner air" before Sunday, but otherwise are seemingly pulling a Los Angeles Rams and just showing up on site the day before the game. The 49ers dominated the Rams in Australia in Week 1, 27-7, and part of that was because their travel plans were so much better. The 49ers have won and covered in four straight International games. … Prediction: 49ers 26, Vikings 20 Dubin (49ers -3): In a battle of a great offense against a great defense, I am usually going to lean toward the offensive side unless there's a really compelling reason in favor of the defensive-minded team. Kirk Cousins' ability to elevate the Vikings' own offense almost provides that reason, but it's not quite enough for me to get there. This San Francisco offense is too much of a well-oiled machine for me to pick against the Niners — even in a matchup with a defensive coordinator as crazy and as good as Brian Flores. … Prediction: 49ers 23, Vikings 17 Cincinnati Bengals (-6.5) at Washington Commanders (MNF) Dajani (Bengals -6.5): Before you think this is some easy pick to make just because of how hot the Bengals are, know that Cincy is 0-2-1 in its past three games against the Washington Commanders , who just upset the Giants in New York last week. Jayden Daniels ' coming-out party as a rookie actually came against the Bengals. Still, it's hard to go against my Super Bowl pick and my MVP pick this season. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Plus, how to watch, what to know and a prediction before the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup Getty Images In the Week 11 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the Houston Texans play host to the division rival Indianapolis Colts . Houston enters this game coming off a dispiriting loss to the Cleveland Browns that dropped the Texans to just 3-6 on the season and dealt a significant blow to their playoff hopes. The Texans need to start stacking wins, and they need to do it right now if they want to make a run at a back-end postseason spot. The Colts, meanwhile, snapped a five-game losing streak with a close win over the Miami Dolphins last week. They didn't exactly light the world on fire, though, and have the look of a team that is just playing out the string after their series of trades ahead of the deadline. Will the Texans bounce back, or will the Colts make it two in a row? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Follow the game live here Where to watch Texans vs. Colts live Date: Thursday, Nov. 19 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ET Location: NRG Stadium (Houston) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Texans -12.5, O/U 44.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Colts have the ball The Texans defense has been one of the most disappointing units in the league this season. Houston ranks 20th in yards allowed, 18th in points allowed and 22nd in EPA per play, according to Tru Media. The Texans checked in first in yards, second in scoring and third in EPA per play a year ago, and were expected to again field one of the top defenses in the league this season after returning almost all of their key pieces. Instead, Houston has struggled to contain opposing passing attacks, repeatedly leaking on the back end despite putting pressure on quarterbacks at an above-average rate. Players like Kamari Lassiter have regressed significantly, while Reed Blankenship has been a bust as a free-agent signing. Luckily for the Texans, they are about to face one of the most inept passing offenses in the NFL . Daniel Jones has been entirely unable to drive the ball in intermediate and deep areas of the field since returning from his Achilles tear, and it has neutered the entire aerial attack. Jones has completed a career-low 59.6% of his passes at a career-low 5.6 yards per attempt, with just seven touchdowns against a league-high 12 interceptions. The Colts also traded away both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen last week, leaving them with Laquon Treadwell , Ashton Dulin , Anthony Gould and Deion Burks as their main wide receivers. There is not an imposing player in the bunch. The Texans should be able to shut down this passing offense with relative ease -- especially if they can get pressure on Jones, who can no longer evade the rush like he did last season. He's already been sacked more times than he was a year ago despite playing three fewer games. The Colts have turned the dial down on Jonathan Taylor 's workload in recent weeks, having him split snaps and carries with rookie Seth McGowan , including in the red zone. Taylor played 81.2% of the offensive snaps through the Colts' first six games, according to Pro-Football Reference, but is at just 66.5% of the snaps since then, with McGowan's usage ticking up. Taylor has also not been as effective this season (career-low 4.2 yards per carry) as in recent years, which isn't surprising given the total lack of a passing game and the Colts' offensive line issues. Those issues should persist on Thursday, with both of Indianapolis' starting tackles out for this game. It's fairly difficult to run on the Texans to begin with (4.0 yards per carry allowed), and it should be even more so with the Colts in their current state. When the Texans have the ball C.J. Stroud is playing the best ball of his career, including his rookie year. Stroud checks in sixth in the NFL in EPA per dropback, according to Tru Media, despite the fact that he's been working with an injured and rotating pass-catcher corps for much of the season. The Colts are an easy bunch to throw on, checking in 27th in the league in net yards per attempt allowed (which accounts for sack yardage), and they won't have Charvarius Ward in this game and may not have Sauce Gardner , either. Nico Collins should see favorable matchups on the outside and be able to feast all night long. The likes of Tank Dell and Xavier Hutchinson could get in the mix as well, though they tend to rotate more heavily in and out of the lineup and therefore see fewer targets than Collins. It's also quite easy to run on Indy, which has leaked 4.8 yards per carry on the season, 29th in the NFL. The Texans, though, have been entirely unable to run the ball, with neither David Montgomery (who is set to return from injury on Thursday night) nor Woody Marks (who is out with a concussion) able to establish anything resembling success on the ground. Montgomery was averaging a mere 2.7 yards per carry before his injury, and Marks has been at only 3.7 per carry in Monty's absence. This is likely to be a game where the Texans lean heavily on Stroud to establish a lead, then turn to the ground game to run the clock out, in what should be a relatively easy matchup given the state of the Colts' roster. So long as the Texans keep Stroud well protected early on, that strategy should be plenty successful, even if it doesn't necessarily result in a blowout win because the Texans themselves aren't that explosive of an offense. I just don't think the Texans should be favored by 12.5 points over anybody. Based on how the odds are looking heading into this contest , many are expecting the night to be a bit one-sided in the hands of the Texans on their home field on a short week. But as with any divisional matchup in the NFL, there's always bound to be some unexpected surprises to unfold that make the events pan out a bit differently than the general consensus expects. With that in mind, let's sort through a batch of three bold predictions on how Thursday night's action could look between the Texans and Colts: Daniel Jones Throws Three Interceptions Sep 27, 2026; Indianapolis, Indiana, USA; Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones (17) drops back to pass against the Houston Texans in the second half at Lucas Oil Stadium. It's hard to imagine the Texans winning the turnover battle 3-0 and still coming up short once again. On the other hand, it might not be too tough to picture Jones struggling with his ball security in another matchup against this defense, especially when factoring in a short week on the road without many reliable weapons in his arsenal of pass-catchers. On the season, Jones is averaging nearly two turnovers a game between his league-leading 12 interceptions and five fumbles. If the Texans take an early lead, and the game script forces the Colts to keep throwing the ball, the door could be wide open for Houston to capitalize on multiple errors from Indianapolis' signal-caller. That means Houston will have to rely on Anderson to carry a bit more of the load within the pass-rush than usual–– but considering he leads the lead in total sacks through 10 weeks, we know he's more than capable of doing just that. On top of Hunter's absence, though, the Colts will be dealing with some key injuries on their offensive line to starting tackles Bernhard Raimann and Jalen Travis. So Anderson––one of the best pass-rushers the NFL has to offer––will have the opportunity to go up against a pair of backup tackles on the Colts line coming off a short week. Anderson has already had one game this season logging three sacks against the Tennessee Titans in Week 5, and maybe Indianapolis is the next AFC South opponent up to face that same fate on Thursday. In fact, four of their last six games have resulted in Houston getting called for 10 or more penalties. Last weekend against the Cleveland Browns, things got as bad as we've seen this season , as the Texans were called for a season-high 13 penalties and 112 yards. Impressively enough, four of those penalties were caused because of their special teams unit. Could the Texans magically turn a corner in this game and look like a more disciplined, refined unit to limit the penalties? It's always possible. Maybe the solution to those penalty problems finally clicked for DeMeco Ryans and this coaching staff after the events of last weekend. But we're now over halfway into the regular season, and Houston is still dealing with those excessive flags, just as they did over the course of 2025. So it's easy to see how this team could have yet another week of 10 or more penalties, especially on a short week of preparation. Stroud in desperate need of a win at home against Daniel Jones and the Indianapolis Colts. These teams are in two different places in 2026, yet they both only have three wins through the first 10 weeks of the season. Indianapolis traded away several key players at the deadline, including Josh Downs, Keenan Allen, DeForest Buckner, and Quenton Nelson, as the team simply doesn't have the same juice that it did to open the 2025 campaign. Despite that, the Colts have a win over Houston in 2026, and the Texans have struggled against just about everyone this season. Houston is 3-6 through nine games, losing on the road against the Cleveland Browns in Week 10. The Texans blew a 17-0 lead in that matchup, struggling mightily on offense in the second half. While C.J. Stroud has played well in the 2026 season, the Houston defense has not lived up to expectations after it finished No. 1 in EPA/Play during the 2025 campaign. Oddsmakers still have the Texans favored by 12.5 points at home in this AFC South battle. Can Houston get back on track and keep its slim playoff hopes alive? A win on Thursday would go a long way to getting the Texans back in the mix for the No. 7 seed in the AFC. All week long, the SI Betting team shared their favorite picks, player props and predictions for this AFC South matchup. Here's a breakdown of some of our favorites to get you ready to bet on the first primetime matchup in Week 11 of the NFL season. Best NFL Picks and Predictions for Colts vs. Texans Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Indianapolis Colts-Houston Texans OVER 44.5 (-105) – Iain MacMillan Jonathan Taylor OVER 49.5 Rushing Yards (-114) – Peter Dewey Nico Collins Anytime TD (-105) – Peter Dewey Tank Dell OVER 2.5 Receptions (-125) – Peter Dewey All season long, SI Betting’s Iain MacMillan shares his favorite bet for every game in his Road to 272 column . For Thursday Night Football in Week 11, he’s taking the OVER between these AFC South teams: With the spread in the double digits, I have no interest in backing either team. Instead, I'm going to take the OVER. The Texans' offense has been their strength this season. They're now ninth in the league in EPA per play and fourth in that metric since Week 4. C.J. Stroud has also been phenomenal, ranking inside the top eight in almost every quarterback metric since Week 4. Now they'll get to feast against a horrific Colts defense that's 21st in opponent EPA per play. Of course, it's hard to trust the Colts' offense, but it's time for us to continue to assume that the Houston offense is going to turn things around and become the elite unit it was the past few seasons. The biggest red flag in this game is that they're 22nd in opponent rush EPA and 27th in opponent rush success rate, which will feed directly into the Colts' offensive strength with Jonathan Taylor. Jonathan Taylor has seen his snap share dip a bit in recent weeks – playing less than 70 percent of the offensive plays in four games in a row – yet he’s still handled a ton of touches for Indy. Taylor carried the ball 13 times for 46 yards in Week 9 against Dallas and 16 times for 83 yards in Week 10 against Miami. He had 23 carries and cleared this prop in Week 3 against Houston, which is 20th in EPA/Rush and allowing 4.0 yards per carry this season. The Colts star has at least 50 rushing yards in seven of his 10 games this season, picking up at least 45 rushing yards in nine of his games. Taylor is still the safest bet to go off for an Indy team that moved on from both Josh Downs and Keenan Allen at the trade deadline. Houston wideout Nico Collins has found the end zone in back-to-back weeks, and he has five touchdowns in seven appearances in the 2026 season. The clear No. 1 option for this Houston offense through the air, Collins has already seen 55 targets from C.J. Stroud, reeling in 37 of them for 478 yards. He was targeted 16 times in the loss to Cleveland in Week 10, and with the Houston running game struggling in 2026, I expect the offense to rely on Stroud throwing the ball on Thursday. The Colts have allowed 17 passing touchdowns this season, but Collins missed the first meeting against them with an injury. I think he makes his presence felt on Thursday night and scores for the third game in a row. After missing all of last season and the start of the 2026 season recovering from a brutal knee injury, Tank Dell is back – and thriving – with Stroud at quarterback. Dell and Stroud have some great chemistry in their time together in the NFL, and the young receiver has played just under 50 percent of the offensive snaps in back-to-back weeks. In Week 9, Dell had four grabs for 105 yards and a score, receiving nine targets from Stroud. He then followed that up with a three-catch game (on four targets) against Cleveland. picks.blurb: Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football NFL Week 11 | Latest updates College football winners/losers Wemby drops 50 ... again Current win 1st title Colts cut Daniel Jones Houston Texans vs Indianapolis Colts: Predictions HOUSTON, TEXAS - SEPTEMBER 17: C.J. Stroud #7 of the Houston Texans runs withe ball during the second half against the Indianapolis Colts at NRG Stadium on September 17, 2023 in Houston, Texas. (Photo by Bob Levey/Getty Images) | Getty Images Mike Bullock · SB Nation Thu, November 19, 2026 at 3:01 PM UTC · 4 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads Here we have 2 teams both racing for the basement – the 3-7 Indianapolis Colts and the 3-6 Houston Texans. The Colts traded away most of their key players to start a rebuild, while the Texans trotted out a failed offensive scheme and altered the winning defensive scheme from 2025. 1 team wants to lose, the other wants to win – but loses anyway. The baby horses currently lead the all-time series, 33-15-1 thanks in great part to the Peyton Manning/Marvin Harrison Sr. years. However, Houston has won 5 of past 6, thanks to the Colts no longer showing interest in winning football. On paper, as of this writing, the Texans should absolutely dominate this game – and very well may. H-Town QB C.J. Stroud is having an MVP season. The Houston wide receiver corps is one of the best in the league – including the son of the aforementioned Harrison Sr.. Their run game ran away when Joe Mixon suffered the mystery of the ages injury in 2024, but Stroud has still managed to find ways to complete 201 passes for 2462 yards, 19 touchdowns and only 3 INTs. The offensive line remains offensive, mostly, but has had just enough get-in-the-way-ness to give Stroud time to throw. Currently, the Texans passing attack is 4th overall. Defensively, Houston has the horsepower to compete at an elite level, but due to off-coverage, injuries and what looks to be confusion with the gameplan, they're currently ranked 20th. Some believe it's a little too much "read your own press coverage", others blame coaching and play calling. In some ways it seems a desire to change up from last season to keep opponents guessing has taken this defense away from what they do best. If you're great at zigging, but decide to zag all the time cause you think your opponent is expecting the zig, then you need to be ok with ignoring your own strengths… We won't talk about the special teams… #ulcerinducing Meanwhile, over in the baby horse stable, the Colts are clearly trotting down the rebuild trail. So far in 2026 Indy has: A new owner who has taken direct control over the coaching staff An interim general manager (after firing their previous one late last month) Quenton Nelson: Traded to the Seattle Seahawks. DeForest Buckner: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. Josh Downs: Traded to the Kansas City Chiefs. Keenan Allen: Traded to the San Francisco 49ers. And managed to win 1 game since all these team-affecting moves. Their current goal seems to be the #1 draft pick, if the Los Angeles Chargers don't beat them to it. Colts vs Texans predictions: In true Houston Texans fashion, the Texans will beat an opponent who doesn't want to win. Just as they did to the aforementioned Chargers. The 2026 brand of Texans football doesn't defeat winning teams (exception: the Jacksonville Jaguars cause, #Glitter). They do, however, lose the battle to not win – meaning when an opponent wants to lose, they freely allow H-Town to go to town on them. Which will happen again tonight. Stroud will look like an MVP candidate on a national stage. The Colts will show all their dysfunction. And the talking heads will ignore the apparent incoming mutiny on Kirby Drive. Indianapolis Colts 13 Houston Texans 38 Those with a superficial knowledge of the Texans will beat the drum that they still have a shot at the playoffs, and how they've fixed their issues. Until the following week when they lose against the Baltimore Ravens at the end of the month. Meanwhile, those who do lift the hood and look beyond the check engine light glaring on this franchise's dashboard will see a different prediction: The end game pot is on the stove, simmering away. Chances are tonight will turn the burn down just long enough to have a nice Thanksgiving.

home.headline: Texans Have Two Offensive Injuries to Monitor After TNF Win
home.blurb: According to an update from the Texans during Thursday night's game, wide receiver Kayshon Boutte (hip) and offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge (stinger) would be deemed questionable for a return in the fourth quarter. We ultimately wound up seeing neither return to the action. But given that the Texans were so close to ending the game, it's unclear as to whether or not either player was dealing with a serious injury issue, or were simply being held out for precautionary reasons as the result of the game had already been decided. Rutledge was cleared to return on a short week against the Colts, but now after the same injury has surfaced once again, there might be a slim chance that Houston's first-round rookie is set to miss a little more time moving forward. As for Boutte, his hip injury seems to be a new issue to surface throughout Thursday night, which turned out to be a pretty successful night on his behalf. The Houston Texans put together a commanding win over the Indianapolis Colts on Thursday night en route to a 26-3 victory that might just be the spark needed to help this team rattle off a few wins in a row through the second half of their season. However, in the midst of the Texans winning effort over the Colts, the team also saw their offense suffer a pair of injuries that will be worth keeping an eye on as they approach their next matchup. However, seeing both Boutte and Rutledge go down with an injury––each of whom has their respective key roles on the Texans' offense––is less than an ideal end to an overall successful night for Houston altogether. Kayshon Boutte, Keylan Rutledge Have Injuries to Keep Watch Of One of these injuries has been an issue the Texans have already seen surface earlier in the month, and that's the stinger that Rutledge suffered that makes for his second stinger in the past two weeks. The first stinger for Rutledge was bad enough that it led to him being sidelined for an entire week of the Texans' team practice , along with missing Week 10's game against the Cleveland Browns, forcing fourth-round rookie Febechi Nwaiwu into his first-ever start. Boutte converted on both of his targets against the Colts for two catches, 40 yards, and an aggressive touchdown reception in the second quarter for C.J. Stroud's second of three touchdown passes on the night––making for his second game on the season where he's seen over 40 yards in a single game. If Boutte is forced to miss any time, it'd mark yet another injury to the Texans’ wide receiver room following up on Jaylin Noel's injured reserve designation before Week 8 , along with the recent absence of Marvin Harrison Jr., which has led to him missing the last two games against the Browns and the Colts. The Buffalo Bills stashed away two former first-round draft picks on their practice squad exactly for a time like this. Slated to host a divisional game against the Miami Dolphins in Week 11, the Bills ruled out defensive starters Christian Benford and Dorian Williams due to injuries. In response to those injury designations, Buffalo tabbed cornerback Tre'Davious White and linebacker Shaq Thompson as practice squad elevations for the first time this season. Meanwhile, the Dolphins will have plenty of backups on the offensive side of the ball on Sunday. Starting running back Devon Achane and quarterback Malik Willis are both unavailable. That means Ollie Gordon will shoulder the bulk of the work on the ground while former Syracuse starter Kyle McCord fills in at quarterback. In other Bills' news on Saturday, defensive tackle Ed Oliver woke up with oblique discomfort. As a result, Buffalo added him to the official injury report with a questionable tag. When did Tre'Davious White rejoin Bills? After starting 16 regular season games last year , White, a 2017 first-round pick by Buffalo, failed to garner overwhelming interest on the free-agent market. With the Bills keeping only three true outside cornerbacks on their 53-man roster, it always made sense to bring White back as an insurance policy, and they finally did on October 19 . "We brought Tre back here, if given the opportunity, to go in there and help us play winning football. I thought he played really good football at the end of last season," said Bills' head coach Joe Brady. away.headline: Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More
away.blurb: The issue at wide receiver is that rookie Caleb Douglas joined the list of injured players at that position as he was limited with a shoulder injury. There was good news there, though, with Chris Bell back at practice (albeit on a limited basis) after both he and Jared Wayne missed the game against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Along with the five players who didn't practice, the Dolphins had five others who were limited. Besides Bell and Douglas, there was LS Tucker Addington again (shoulder), CB JuJu Brents (neck) and C Andrew Meyer (neck). The Bills also had five players sit out practice Wednesday, with guard O'Cyrus Torrence's absence related to a personal issue. Furthermore, three safeties were limited in practice, including recent acquisition Amani Hooker (knee) along with Damar Hamlin (toe) and Cole Bishop (shoulder). Dolphins First Week 11 Injury Report: Brewer Status Quo, Punter Problem, and More Skip to main content SI.COM Center Aaron Brewer missing another practice as he remains in the concussion protocol clearly was the biggest headline of the Miami Dolphins' first injury report for Week 11, but there are several other issues worth monitoring. The most glaring ones would be at wide receiver, where injuries continue to happen, and at punter. The situation with punter Bradley Pinion missing practice because a right groin injury maybe shouldn't have been easy to predict after the Dolphins signed punter Jack Browning to the practice squad earlier Wednesday. As a general rule, NFL teams don't have two punters or two kickers on the team (active roster and practice squad) unless there's an injury, so the Browning move should have been a sign. As we indicated earlier, Browning has appeared in five NFL games but none since the 2024 season and hasn't even punted in a preseason since then. Wayne was among the five players who didn't practice, a group that included safety Dante Trader Jr. (shoulder/groin) and cornerback Jaylin Simpson (knee). Trader has been battling injuries for a few weeks now and one wonders whether he'll need to be shut down at some point to allow him to get back to 100 percent. While it's early in the week, the best projection if Trader can't play against Buffalo would be for Zayne Anderson to get the start alongside rookie Michael Taaffe even if Kyle Louis has been getting regular snaps on defense since coming off IR. Louis has been used as a type of nickel linebacker as opposed to a true safety. Simpson is primarily a special teams contributor, and if Wayne can't play again, then it would mean another game for veteran Jalen Tolbert. In the event that both Brewer and Meyer wound up sidelined for the Buffalo game, then we'd be looking at Jarrett Kingston, who played center for two snaps against the Colts when Meyer briefly left the game. The focus for Buffalo should be in the secondary, which was missing Wednesday cornerbacks Dee Alford (concussion) and Christian Benford (groin). Published Nov 18, 2026 ALAIN POUPART Ala

picks.blurb: Saints vs. Bears: Staff Picks and Score Predictions for Sunday Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The New Orleans Saints (3-6) face another difficult challenge Sunday when they travel to Soldier Field to take on the Chicago Bears (7-2). Coming off a disappointing loss to the Carolina Panthers , the Saints continue to struggle with offensive consistency and finishing games under head coach Kellen Moore. Those problems could prove costly against a well-rounded Chicago team that boasts one of the NFL's most productive offenses and a top-10 defense. Can the Saints pull off an unlikely upset, or will their struggles continue against one of the NFC's top contenders? Here's how our staff predicts Sunday's matchup will unfold. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 28-14 This is a game that doesn’t favor the Saints. The Bears are by far the best team the Saints have faced since the Detroit Lions , who beat New Orleans in overtime. They have one of the league’s best offenses , led by quarterback Caleb Williams , and one of the league's most balanced teams. Defensively, the Bears have a top-10 defense. Chicago boasts a top-10 defense, ranking eighth in scoring (20.4 PPG) and seventh in total defense (310.9 YPG). Their strength lies against the run, allowing 91.1 yards per game (seventh-fewest), while placing 15th against the pass (219.8 YPG). Crucially, the Bears lead the NFL in third-down defense (22.8% conversion rate allowed) and rank 12th in red-zone touchdown efficiency (53.8%). They maintain consistent pass pressure with 26 sacks (ninth) and seven interceptions (tied for 11th). Also, this will be the first cold-weather game for the Saints as the temperature will be in the 50s throughout the game. I don’t think the Saints will pull off the upset, but what I do know is that the Saints have played better on the road as both of their wins came on the road against the Baltimore Ravens and New York Giants . I do think its defense will do enough to make this game tight before Chicago pulls away near the end. Prediction : Bears 28 Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: L 32-21 This is a Saints team that seems to be searching, searching for an identity, a consistent offense, people on the same page. The New Orleans offense sputters and coughs more than my old 1969 VW Beetle. No matter what I would do to that little air-cooled engine, it never could quite get started, and when it did, it usually took a few minutes of driving before it would get going smoothly. Once it was warmed up, that little thing was a joy to drive. Unfortunately, it took a while to even get to that point. The Saints O reminds me of that Beetle. They can't seem to get going in the beginning. Once they get warmed up and going, they are fun to watch. Until then, it's almost torturous to be a part of. Eventually, I had to get rid of that little car. Keeping the valves aligned properly on that rapidly expanding air-cooled engine proved to be one of those "I'll be doing this forever" kind of projects, so I just gave up and moved on. The New Orleans offense is at that point, in my opinion. A squad that cannot consistently move the ball, stopping and starting itself with poor run blocking, or wide receivers and a quarterback who aren't on the same page, or play calling that comes across as vanilla as can be (think runs in the middle). Now, Brandon Staley's group is another story, another car if you will. They remind me of a Tesla. The Saints defense can really get going with the first acceleration, but fade at the end. A battery-powered Tesla is a lot like that. They can fly right out the gate and tear the street up, but don't expect that to last, as those batteries won't go 300-plus miles (no matter what they say) like a gas-power engine will, losing energy much sooner than their gas counterparts. This Saints defense has produced through the first three quarters, especially for the last few games. Although getting turnovers has been a notable absence for this group, it has played well, up until the final quarter. To wit, the Panthers' game. I say all that to say this: you cannot do any of what the offense and defense has been doing against a quality team. The Panthers, Browns, and Steelers were not quality teams. This Bears team is. It will take a complete game, start to finish, for this Saints team to have a chance to beat Chicago. The local boys haven't done that all year long. Prediction : Bears 32 Saints 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . He returned to the Big Easy after serving as the lead beat reporter for North Carolina Tar Heels On SI. away.headline: New Orleans Saints injury report: Five ruled out; Tyson good to go
away.blurb: The Saints will be without five players Sunday at Soldier Field, and the list hits the offensive line and the secondary hardest. New Orleans ruled out center Erik McCoy (biceps), right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee), tackle Asim Richards (knee), cornerback Martin Emerson (concussion), and safety Justin Reid (personal matter). None of the five practiced at all this week, so none of these come as a surprise, and Reid’s personal matter is the technical term for him being released by the team. The offensive line losses stand out most. Three linemen are out, including McCoy and Fuaga, and that’s a lot of reshuffling up front against a Bears defense that sacked Baker Mayfield four times in its last game. The back end is banged up, too. With Emerson and Reid out, cornerback Decamerion Richardson (thigh) is questionable after being limited all week. Linebacker Pete Werner (hamstring) is also questionable, even though he didn’t practice once after leaving the Carolina game. Questionable after three missed practices usually leans toward sitting, so I wouldn’t count on Werner. Either way, Caleb Williams should see a thinner coverage group than usual. The Saints did get some good news. Rookie receiver Jordyn Tyson (chest) was upgraded to a full practice Friday after two limited days. Alvin Kamara practiced fully after a rest day Wednesday, and running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) fully participated all week. All three carry no game designation. Linebacker Isaiah Stalbird missed Friday’s practice for a personal matter but also has no designation. The New Orleans Saints submitted their final injury report of the week on Thursday ahead of their Week 11 contest with the Chicago Bears. away.headline: Is Jordyn Tyson playing today? Latest update on Saints WR vs. Bears
away.blurb: What's the word on Jordyn Tyson? The New Orleans Saints rookie wideout was limited at practice to start the week, which was concerning. He spent months recovering from a hamstring injury after another hamstring issue cost him most of his first NFL offseason. He's going to be under the microscope anytime his name appears on the injury report. At least this wasn't another hamstring. Tyson picked up a chest injury coming out of last week's game with the Carolina Panthers , in which he caught 11 receptions, which meant he was limited at practice for most of the week. But he practiced fully on Friday and has no game status listed for Sunday's kickoff with the Chicago Bears . Expect him to be full-go at Soldier Field. The Saints will need him. They've only scored five touchdowns across their last three games, with head coach Kellen Moore slipping into even more predictable opening scripts as the pressure builds on him to deliver. We know Tyson will get his targets, if last week's game was any indication (and you'd assume he plays even more snaps after doubling his reps from his first game to his second). The challenge seems to be managing three different receivers and a pass-catching tight end in Juwan Johnson. Whether it's Moore calling plays or Tyler Shough spreading the ball around, the Saints haven't done a good enough job keeping Johnson and veteran wideout Devaughn Vele involved in the offense since Tyson made his debut. To that end, they haven't even gotten Chris Olave going early; his first catch last week came late in the second quarter. It's great that Tyson is ready to play. But he won't turn the season around on his own. If the Saints don't have the coach and quarterback in place to take advantage of all of these weapons, they'll have to find someone who can. Between deadline trades that added strength to the franchise's rebuild and promising development from young players across the board, the Robert Saleh era is slowly building into something fans can get behind. In Week 11, his Titans team has a chance to win their second game of the season on the road vs. the Dallas Cowboys. Here's one reason they'll get it done, one reason they'll fall short, and my own prediction for how things will ultimately pan out. Will: Cam Ward, Tony Pollard have big games The Cowboys, after allowing 46 points to the San Francisco 49ers in a loss last week, just turned over defensive play-calling duties to senior assistant coach Mike Pettine. Dallas' defense is struggling, and if the Titans win, it'll be because Cam Ward and Tony Pollard take advantage of that. Ward has been on a short tear as of late, doubling his touchdown total through seven games in the last two. The second-season QB has also eclipsed 200 yards in back-to-back games for the first time this year. With WR Carnell Tate likely to return, Ward is tracking for another leap. On the ground, meanwhile, the Cowboys' rushing defense is last in the league in yards allowed per game (154.1) and yards per carry (5.2). This marks Pollard's first game against his former team; the numbers are supportive, and the stakes are there. The Titans' offense has simply been on a team-wide heater as of late. It'll take another inspired performance from key playmakers to pull it off, but Tennessee has a clear angle to a road win. Won't: Titans' defense continues downward spiral However, Tennessee's defense has been trending in the opposite direction. As has been the case in the past two weeks, Saleh's bunch have mostly erased positive offensive momentum and cost the Titans' two chances at winnable games. If Tennessee were to fall short in Week 11, I have to think it would be for the same reason. On the road after arguably their worst showing of the year, Saleh's defense has their back against the wall. Prediction: Titans win, 30-27 With that said, I still think the Titans find a way to pull this one out. If the away team can strike a balance between their growing offensive attack and a defense that isn't allowing Dallas to do whatever they want, a close win is in the cards. The Titans have yet to play a full, complete game this year. Even their Week 6 victory over the Indianapolis Colts saw Tennessee trailing 13-0 at halftime. I'm predicting that the Titans get this done, and do so by offering a solid showing through all four quarters. That means a consistent Cam Ward, a defense that bends, but doesn't break, reliable play-calling on either side of the ball, and at least a little good luck on the injury front. away.headline: Report: Titans pass rusher involved in severe vehicle incident before Week 11 showdown
away.source: Last Word On Sports on MSN
away.blurb: Reports emerged on Saturday afternoon that an injured Tennessee Titans pass rusher was involved in a serious vehicle accident. Initial reports indicated that Jaylen Harrell was involved in the accident and was hospitalized with injuries. However, later reporting that Harrell’s level of involvement escalated into potential assault. Report: Titans Pass Rusher Involved In Severe Vehicle Incident Before Week 11 Showdown Authorities are investigating the circumstances of the allegations against the Titans pass rusher involved in the accident, so nothing substantive can be said yet. This is the third serious incident involving a Titans player in recent months. Calvin Ridley allegedly committed assault in Nashville, and Jordan Elliott was released after attempting to retrieve a firearm following an altercation with OT J.C. Latham. Ridley’s case is still being adjudicated, while Elliott landed another tryout opportunity with the Chicago Bears. The Titans released a boilerplate statement wishing Harrell and his family well after the accident, but revealed nothing before the seriousness of the allegations emerged. Now that the allegations are public, the league office and the franchise must do their due diligence. The Titans pass rusher has imperiled his career if these are ultimately proven true. This is the first known off-field incident that Harrell has been involved in since he entered the NFL as a seventh-round selection in the 2024 draft. Harrell landed on injured reserve during the 2026 preseason with an ACL injury, ending his season before it began. In two seasons, he has produced 38 tackles, seven tackles for loss, and 4.5 sacks as a key reserve for the Titans. He was expected to contribute meaningful reps as a backup in 2026, but the injury made it impossible. The allegations are serious enough to warrant a further look by the franchise and league, as the Titans pass rusher involved himself to a degree that a second car was part of the incident. He allegedly assaulted the driver from the backseat, which caused the original vehicle to hit a second one and resulted in damage to a light pole in the end. As a result of the accident, Harrell was thrown forward against the windshield with enough force to require hospitalization. If he is found guilty of what is alleged, jail time is certainly on the table. Financially, the Titans would take a dead cap hit of $ 1,190,000 if he is released during the 2027 offseason, with cap savings of $20,184. It isn’t a huge number that could affect signings in the near future, but a mere rounding error on the cap sheet. As a former seventh-round selection still on his rookie contract, Harrell’s contract is a pittance to absorb easily. More than likely, he will get suspended and/or cut once the authorities, league, and the franchise complete the investigation. The Titans pass rusher involved in the accident could see his aspiring career end before it really could ascend into meaningful reps, due to his own doing. Harre

away.blurb: The Dallas Cowboys defense was playing its best football of the year against the Tennessee Titans in Sunday's Week 11 game — even with one of its starters out with an injury. Cowboys inside linebacker Dee Winters was forced to leave the game in the first half with a leg injury, and the Cowboys were up 20-3 early in the second quarter. "Dee Winters helped off the field, and it looks like he's going back to the locker room," Fox Sports color commentator and former NFL tight end Greg Olsen said during the broadcast. "Update: Dee Winters is being helped off the field by Cowboys medical staff, unable to put weight on his leg," Cowboys reporter Patrik Walker wrote on his official X account on Sunday. In 8 games, Winters has 8 starts with 43 tackles, 1 interception, 1 fumble recovery, and 3 TFL. Cowboys Just Made Huge Change on Defense The Cowboys are playing their first game since making a major defensive change, when playcalling duties were taken away from 1st-year defensive coordinator Christian Parker and handed to special defensive assistant Mike Pettine. That move came as the Cowboys sat at 4-6 and came off a 46-40 loss to the San Francisco 49ers in Week 10, when Dallas gave up a franchise-record 584 yards of total offense. The Cowboys made the 34-year-old Parker the NFL's youngest defensive coordinator when they hired him in January after seven seasons as a defensive assistant — including the last two seasons with the Philadelphia Eagles, which included a Super Bowl win following the 2024 season. From ESPN's Todd Archer : "Christian Parker said he considered not remaining with the Cowboys, but, ‘in my opinion, that would have been running from it.' Called a ‘significant,' personal disappointment and said the new arrangement is ‘only awkward if you make it that way.'" A potential battle for first-place in the NFC North looms on Thursday, but Detroit needs to stay in that race with a win on Sunday. The Buccaneers are having a down year by their standards, but are showing signs of life since Baker Mayfield returned to action three weeks ago. Mayfield is on track to play this week, but is banged up with a foot injury that could limit his mobility. Even without Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions should be able to get after the hampered Mayfield and put Tampa Bay's offense in tough situations. Even though the Lions could struggle to run the ball, I think they can find enough big plays in the passing game to avoid a trap game and win another close game to set up next week's massive showdown. Lions 27, Buccaneers 23 I believe the Lions will be tested more than you would think on Sunday against the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers. While the Buccaneers’ passing game has basically been non-existent, their run game has been ultra proficient with Bucky Irving leading the way. Plus, their run defense has been the best in the league, allowing just 712 yards through the season's first 10 weeks. Subsequently, Jahmyr Gibbs will face a stiff challenge against Todd Bowles’ squad, and likely will have one of his weaker games, statistically speaking, of the 2026 campaign. Yet, I still believe he will pop off a couple of big runs. And on top of that, I believe that Lions defensive tackle Alim McNeill will deliver a “plus” effort, as both a run defender and a pass-rusher. So, even without Aidan Hutchinson, I believe that defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard won't allow the banged-up Baker Mayfield to get too comfortable in the pocket. As a result, I believe Dan Campbell's squad will do just enough to secure the Week 11 win. Lions 31, Buccaneers 21 John Maakaron The Lions are facing a stiff test this week, as the Buccaneers are the best team defending the run and rushing the football. For Todd Bowles' squad, the offense cannot pass the football effectively, no matter what it tries. Detroit features one of the worst pass defenses, but has been clamping down at the right times. Jared Goff will look to end his interception streak by distributing the football evenly to his weapons. Even if Jahmyr Gibbs does not have a strong game, the Lions can score points, especially after making halftime adjustments. They're well-rested off their bye week, but they're set to face off against a strong 7-2 Detroit Lions team on the road in what could be the toughest remaining game on the schedule. The Bucs themselves are 3-6, but despite that, they remain one game back from the NFC South lead. The defense has been elite and the run game has been stout, but the passing offense has been a big problem for Tampa Bay — and it may not get much better, as quarterback Baker Mayfield is set to play this game while dealing with a painful plantar fascia injury. As always, we've rounded up our staff to lock in our picks for Sunday's game. Can the Bucs pull off the upset? Or will they fall to 3-7? Caleb Skinner, Writer: Lions 20, Bucs 17 It's getting to the point for the Bucs that they must win, or their season could be over. And things don't get easier this week as they take on the Lions. The Lions own one of the NFL's elite offenses and will test the Bucs' top-rated defense. It's unlikely they'll replicate their turnover margin as they did against the Bears, but they can most definitely slow Detroit down. While the defense won't be too much of a worry, the problems will once again come on the offensive side of the ball for Tampa Bay. The Lions' defense has stepped it up in recent weeks, and even without Aidan Hutchinson, they should be able to stymie the offense enough. I expect this one to be a low-scoring affair at Ford Field, with the Lions coming away with a close home victory to drop the Bucs to 3-7 on the year. Overall Record: 5-4 James Hill, Writer: Lions 24, Bucs 17 Baker Mayfield is once again on the mend from an injury. Yes, the Lions have injuries of their own with Aiden Hutchinson and Jack Campbell, but I don’t know if a hobbled Baker Mayfield or a healthy Jalon Daniels will be able to get the job done. Overall Record: 4-5 Collin Haalboom, Writer: Lions 27, Bucs 21 As much as I believe that the Buccaneers' defense is for real, I also believe the offense is not. Detroit, on the other hand, has one of the most dynamic offenses in the entire league. Beyond just the litany of weapons he has at his disposal, Jared Goff has been extremely effective playing against Bowles' blitz-heavy defenses over the past several years. For the Bucs to win, they'll need to get pressure with four to avoid sending extra guys to disrupt Goff in the pocket. The problem is, even if they do that and manage to generate turnovers like they have been so far this year on defense, the Bucs will need Baker Mayfield to look like a competent NFL QB on offense to win this football game. Sadly, I'm not sure if that version of Mayfield even exists anymore. Overall Record: 6-3 Logan Robinson, Founder: Lions 27, Bucs 20 Another battle for Todd Bowles against a high-scoring offense in Detroit. I’m excited to watch that, but the next thing I’m most intrigued about is the Bucs’ offensive passing attack. That has to improve, or Tampa Bay isn’t making the playoffs — It’s quite simple for me on that. Hopefully the bye week helped, but I’m very cautious about picking the Buccaneers. River Wells, Editor: Lions 24, Bucs 16 The Bucs have a few things going for them, but this is a passing league, and unfortunately, they don't have the passing offense to hang with good teams — much less an elite one like the Lions. The defense will likely hold the Detroit Lions' dynamic offense in check, but the passing offense won't be enough, and it could be even worse than usual with Mayfield's injury. I think the Bucs defense will keep them in it, but it won't be enough to win against a team that could end up winning the brutal NFC North this season. Consensus: Lions 5, Bucs 0 Once again, our staff isn't picking Tampa Bay whatsoever. Our staff unanimously picked the Bears two weeks ago, and we've unanimously picked the Lions here. It's any given Sunday in the NFL, so the Bucs are always in it. But they'll have to convince us that they can beat good teams, and so far, they simply haven't. picks.blurb: Roundtable: Lions Week 11 Preview Against Buccaneers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI The Detroit Lions OnSI staff previews the Detroit Lions Week 11 matchup with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. 1. How much is Aidan Hutchinson to blame for his ACL injury? Christian Booher: I think Hutchinson is definitely deserving of some blame for the fact that the injury occurred in such an unnecessary fashion. The movements that went into that injury have been analyzed, and it's rightfully pointed out that a move like the one he did to celebrate that sack poses a risk. However, it's such a fluke situation that it's hard to be extremely mad at the circumstances. He's done that celebration many times, and it just so happens that he has to learn of the risks this way. Vito Chirco: At the end of the day, it was a freak accident and could've happened to any one of the hundreds of players that celebrate after sacks and other big plays. However, as a defensive captain and veteran player now, he should've known better than to leave his feet to celebrate, especially after his previous season-ending injury just two years ago. Consequently, I believe it's fair to say that Hutchinson deserves to shoulder a fair portion of the blame for the ACL ailment. Emmett Matasovsky: It was not the smartest play by Aidan Hutchinson in that injury, I cannot lie. That said, the amount of negative comments towards the EDGE is a bit extreme this week. When a play like that happens, most players’ ligaments tend to be a few plays from giving during game action, frankly. It was not a smart celebration, especially with previous comments to stop the celebrations that could cause non-contact injuries. I will say it is a 60 percent Hutchinson fault, 40 percent circumstance of being close to a natural injury anyway. 2. Are Buccaneers going to be able to slow down Jahmyr Gibbs? Booher : I think the Lions will find some tough sledding on the ground throughout Sunday's game. The Buccaneers have had success against the Lions in past matchups when it comes to slowing down the run game, and with Vita Vea leading the charge, I think the Lions will once again struggle to run the ball. As a result, I think the key to victory is the right arm of Jared Goff, as he'll need to keep the offense on schedule through the air. Chirco : Despite the Buccaneers’ prowess against the run this season, I believe that Gibbs still ends up with a solid day on the ground. And you know that Drew Petzing will also deploy the dual-threat runner as often as possible as a receiver. I expect Gibbs to be contained a bit, but to still produce a couple of big runs in the Week 11 contest. Matasovsky : With the Buccaneers battered and the Lions with momentum, the best hope for Tampa Bay is that Gibbs has jetlag. I think it will be tough sledding for the Tampa defensive line. Gibbs has hit his stride and is coming off a performance of over 250 yards from scrimmage. The fatigue, especially post-international travel, might lead to more Vaki touches, but I do not see the Bucs stopping the Lions running backs room. 3. Who will be Detroit Lions game MVP? Booher : I think Goff is the MVP on Sunday. As I mentioned, the Lions could really struggle to run the ball, which puts more pressure on Goff and offensive coordinator Drew Petzing to dial up counters. Another player that I think is due for a big day is tight end Sam LaPorta, who will likely match up with former Detroit defensive standout Alex Anzalone throughout Sunday's game. Chirco : I'm going to go with Alim McNeill. The run-stuffing interior lineman has had an ultra productive campaign thus far this season, and he will need to come up big Sunday against Tampa Bay RB Bucky Irving. He also will be counted upon even more now as a pass-rusher due to the season-ending injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson. With all this said, I believe he'll deliver a solid performance against the Buccaneers, keying a sixth straight victory for Detroit. Matasovsky : It would be foolish to not select Gibbs here. Jahmyr Gibbs has a chance to run free and make plays, especially if Yaya Diaby is out. The back will have a phenomenal backing up from his Munich game, with another effort over 100 yards rushing and two total touchdowns. 4. Will Kerby Joseph make a big impact this week? Booher : I'm tempering my expectations for Joseph in his first game of the season. More than anything, I want to see him be pain-free in his return to action. Before he was officially shut down last year, he would often depart games for a series at a time while dealing with this nagging knee injury, and so I want to see him get through the matchup without having to depart due to pain. Chirco : I'm going to say no. I think the All-Pro safety will log 45-50 total defensive snaps in his season debut. But ultimately, I believe he'll show signs of being hampered by his lingering knee issue. I'd temper my expectations from Joseph in this Week 11 matchup. Matasovsky : I can see this going both ways. I could see Kerby Joseph making a huge play, especially against potentially an undrafted rookie quarterback. However, I can also argue that I see Joseph on a “pitch count” and limited reps. Personally, I hope that it is the former, where Joseph announces he is back with an interception and gets his moment to celebrate in front of the home crowd. 5. What do you want to see from DE Ahmed Hassanein in his debut this season? Booher : Hassanein is a player that is easy to root for due to his mentality and his journey to the NFL. It's been a tough road since he was drafted by Detroit last year, but Sunday will be his first chance to prove he belongs. In the big end role that he will likely play, Hassanein needs to be firm in setting the edge, and I think he could also make an impact with a few pressures if he gets opportunities in passing downs. Chirco : I believe it's reasonable to expect Hassanein to garner a couple of QB hits and pressures in his NFL debut on Sunday. He faces a difficult task going up against the slippery Baker Mayfield. However, the Lions will be counting on the Boise State product to make life at least a little bit difficult for the veteran passer. Matasovsky : Hassanein will have a chance to make an impact, but I will settle for the Boise State product at least making a mark on the box score. It is tough to argue that he deserves more reps than a red hot Derrick Moore, who has four sacks in the last two outings. The former Lions sixth-round pick has earned the right to play, and was likely going to get a chance before Hutchinson’s injury prompted the move up the depth chart. That said, now is the time for the Egyptian. I want to see the player do his job and make positive plays, even if it is not a box score-stuffing day. At the end of the day, the second-year pro is a role player, and football is a game where all 11 players doing their job and role means a successful day. Simply put, I want a penalty free, “plus” day from Hassanein. Published 11 hours ago VITO CHIRCO Vito has covered the NFL and the Detroit Lions for the past five years. A trip to Ford Field to face the 7-2 Detroit Lions is a tough place to start fixing that. The quarterback news is better than it looked earlier in the week. Head coach Todd Bowles said Friday that Baker Mayfield is trending in the right direction to start on his sprained foot, according to NBC Sports . Here are four bold predictions for Sunday's noon CT kickoff. 1. Bucky Irving outrushes Jahmyr Gibbs Gibbs leads the NFL with 1,000 rushing yards, and Bowles compared him to Barry Sanders this week. He's also running into the best run defense in the league . Tampa Bay allows 79.1 rushing yards per game, the fewest in the NFL, according to ESPN. We compared each back's average to what the other defense allows. Gibbs averages 111.1 rushing yards per game, about 32 more than the Bucs give up to entire offenses. Irving averages 91.7 per game on 4.9 yards per carry, almost exactly the 90.4 Detroit allows. On paper, Irving has the easier path. 2. home.blurb: The Lions will operate without starting center Cade Mays once more, who was ruled out in Detroit's Friday injury report . Mays will miss his third straight game after suffering an ankle injury against the Minnesota Vikings in the Lions' Week 8 win. Six other Lions were listed as questionable against the Bucs , including Joe Bachie (knee), cornerback Khalil Dorsey (ankle), defensive lineman Tyler Lacy (shoulder), cornerback Ennis Rakestraw Jr. (shoulder), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip), and running back Sione Vaki (ankle). Safety Kerby Joseph (knee) was a full participant and is expected to make his long-awaited return . The Detroit Lions (7-2) are readying for a Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers (3-6). Detroit is eyeing a sixth straight victory. The 6-foot-6, 325-pound center inked a three-year, $25 million deal with the Lions this offseason, but he's played in just a pair of games. Mays began the season on injured reserve after sustaining a broken right wrist during training camp. Juice Scruggs has played exceptionally well in Mays' absence, ranking as the top center in the NFL per Pro Football Focus . According to PFF , Scruggs has surrendered just one sack and 11 pressures. Lions offensive lineman Miles Frazier wasn't listed on Wednesday or Thursday, but he didn't practice on Friday for personal reasons. home.headline: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury
home.blurb: "Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out." This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Report: Lions' Hutchinson out for season with ACL injury Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16. Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added. On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.” The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee. Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side. Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday. If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

Will that trend continue in Week 11? Visiting head coach Andy Reid's crew are Mike LaFleur and the Arizona Cardinals, who managed to capture two wins in three games earlier this campaign but have since dropped back-to-back outings. Down to their fourth quarterback of the year, their work is cut out for them against a surging Kansas City squad. With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 11 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: In each of the last two weeks, I’ve been able to genuinely argue that the Jets and Falcons were better (or at least more dangerous) than their meager records would indicate. The 3-7 Cardinals are probably worse than their record, especially while they’re preparing to be quarterbacked by a new-in-town 40-year-old super-journeyman. There are no excuses for the Chiefs to stumble in this game. The Chiefs have put up 35 points in each of their last two wins while holding the Jets and Falcons to 12 and 13 points, respectively. With the Buffalo Bills on the horizon, I expect a similarly stout defensive performance, but I wouldn’t be surprised if the Chiefs are content to park the bus offensively if they hold a second-half lead over Arizona. Jordan Foote: Given their recent shellackings of the New York Jets and Atlanta Falcons, it's hard not to think the Chiefs will emerge with a comfortable Week 11 victory over the Cardinals here. Arizona is simply too devoid of talent on either side of the ball, leaving only a bizarre outcome that borders on a miracle being the club's main path to a win. Kansas City's banged-up roster is still miles ahead of Arizona's, with the duo of Patrick Mahomes and Emmett Johnson alone being enough to move the chains. On the other side of the ball, Josh Johnson is an experienced vet, but Steve Spagnuolo may have something in store for him. Give me the Chiefs to roll to 8-2 on the year as the toughest part of their schedule approaches. Joshua Schulman: There’s very little meaningful analysis to provide against an opponent of this caliber. The Cardinals are down several key starters and have been one of the NFL's worst teams over the past handful of weeks. With 40-year-old journeyman Josh Johnson set to fill in for the injured Carson Beck, I’m expecting the Chiefs to steamroll Arizona. Look for Emmett Johnson to have another big game as Kenneth Walker misses his second consecutive game . Tyler Brown: For the third straight week, I think the Chiefs win by three touchdowns. Emmett Johnson could be in line for another career day, and the only thing that may hold him back is a big lead that gets Jadyn Ott into the game. Arizona is ranked 28th in rushing defense. With the offensive line being tinkered with , I expect Patrick Mahomes to experiment with his receiving corps as well. It will be interesting to see whether Josh Downs and Cyrus Allen get a large uptick in snaps, but I am not sure it matters. Any receiver on the depth chart could have a big day against this defense. The Cardinals' offense is as limited as it gets. Trey McBride is their only real weapon, with a wide receiver group where not a single one has topped 100 yards total on the season. Running back Tyler Allgeier is a competent runner but doesn't threaten a defense. Lastly, Josh Johnson, a 19-year veteran journeyman, is under center for a team already on its fourth quarterback. Pictured: Patrick Mahomes. This article contains predictions for an old game. The Kansas City Chiefs (7-2) will host the Arizona Cardinals (3-7) in Week 11 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Arrowhead Stadium in Kansas City, Missouri. The game will broadcast live on CBS. The Chiefs are 15.5-point favorites over the Cardinals on the spread, with the total set at over/under 40.5 points. Kansas City is a -1500 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Arizona is a +870 underdog to pull off the road upset. Let's get into my Cardinals vs Chiefs predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 22. They are decimated by injuries right now, particularly along the offensive line, where they have been down to second and third-stringers across the board. The results for quarterback Carson Beck were entirely predictable in his first professional start last week. He struggled under pressure during his college career, and it is translating exactly the same way to the NFL. Last week, he was pressured six times and took a sack on five of those dropbacks. Beck will have to wait to make his second start as the rookie was ruled out with a back injury. This forces journeyman backup Josh Johnson into action against a Chiefs defense that is highly adept at generating pressure. The only reliable weapon Johnson has is tight end Trey McBride . While the Chiefs rank 24th in the league against tight ends, defensive coordinator Steve Spagnuolo can easily just double team McBride all game because Arizona has no other threats at the wide receiver position to make them pay on the outside. Defensively, however, the Cardinals have been surprisingly feisty against the run. They currently rank in the top 10 in defensive rush DVOA and are second overall in rush EPA allowed. Kansas City Chiefs Preview: Classic Lookahead Spot for KC The Chiefs find themselves in a classic lookahead spot with a titanic AFC clash against the Bills looming on deck on Thanksgiving. In a week where they are laying over two touchdowns against a decimated Cardinals team, the last thing Chiefs head coach Andy Reid wants to do is show anything exotic on tape or risk getting his key contributors hurt. We saw Patrick Mahomes look spectacular last week, and Josh Downs looks like a seamless addition to this offense. Mahomes was driving the ball downfield without showing any signs of elbow issues, and his metrics were off the charts. Emmett Johnson also shined in a spot start for the injured Kenneth Walker III, who has not practiced all week and is looking unlikely to play in this game. However, because of the situational spot, I am expecting a vanilla game plan from Kansas City. Once they secure an early lead, the Chiefs are going to run the ball and chew the clock. I expect to see Kansas City orchestrate methodical, nine-minute drives that bleed the clock dry, similarly to how it closed out the Falcons last week. The Chiefs can essentially name their score, but their primary goal will be shortening the game and getting to Thanksgiving healthy. Without any wide receivers to stretch the field, the Chiefs should be able to neutralize Trey McBride. On the other side, Kansas City has no incentive to run up the score or utilize its best offensive concepts with the Bills on deck on Thanksgiving. The Chiefs will lean on the run game — which Arizona actually defends reasonably well — and grind the clock into dust. I expect a fast-moving second half with very few points. away.headline: Carson Beck Injured, Latest Updates on Cardinals QB's Status vs. Chiefs for NFL Week 11
away.blurb: Carson Beck has been downgraded to out for Sunday because of back spasms. On Friday, Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur told reporters Friday he was preparing to start Johnson after Beck did not practice due to a back injury. After not being listed on the injury report Wednesday, Beck was added on Thursday, as he was a limited participant in practice. The third-round pick out of Miami struggled to get much going in a 34-6 loss to the Rams, completing 11 of his 18 passing attempts for 108 yards with no touchdowns and two interceptions, while also getting sacked five times. The Arizona Cardinals will turn to veteran backup quarterback Josh Johnson when they face the Kansas City Chiefs. After the Cardinals traded Jacoby Brissett to the Baltimore Ravens and Gardner Minshew suffered a season-ending UCL injury, Beck made his first career NFL start against the Los Angeles Rams this past Sunday. Arizona signed Johnson off the Cincinnati Bengals' practice squad following the Minshew injury, and he may now be in line to start just a couple of weeks later. Johnson, 40, has spent time with numerous teams over the course of his lengthy NFL career, and the Cardinals could become the eighth different team with which he has seen regular-season action. Over 50 career NFL games, including 11 starts, Johnson is 2-9, and he has completed 58.7 percent of his passing attempts for 2,669 yards, 14 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. Johnson made two starts for the Washington Commanders last season, posting a 1-1 record. Even with Beck in the lineup, the 3-7 Cardinals were going to be massive underdogs on the road against a 7-2 Chiefs team that is battling with the Denver Broncos for the AFC West lead.
