away.headline: Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck
away.blurb: "Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday. The Cardinals stuck true to their word, as Beck was listed as questionable on the team's official Friday injury report. OUT - Zach Carter (knee), Jon Gaines (ankle) QUESTIONABLE - Carson Beck (back) Carter remains out while working through his 21-day practice window in his return from injured reserve while Gaines practiced Wednesday but not Thursday/Friday before being ruled out. Beck carried no injury designation after his rookie debut, practiced fine on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday, which raised some concerns. OUT - Jaylon Moore (ankle), Trey Smith (concussion), Kenneth Walker (groin) QUESTIONABLE - Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), Peter Woods (neck) None of Kansas City's three players marked out practiced in any capacity this week while both Norman-Lott and Woods hit the field for all three days in some capacity. Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are holding on to hope. Carson Beck is not expected to be the team's starting quarterback when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11 thanks to a back injury that popped up this week. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center. The picture for both sides entering Week 11: Arizona Cardinals Injury Report Now, barring an eye-opening turnaround, Beck is set to be sidelined. Kansas City Chiefs Injury Report This is the second time Beck suffered a back injury, as earlier in the regular season the rookie quarterback was listed on Arizona's injury report with the same issue that's now flaring up once again. "I can't answer that because you just treat it," LaFleur told reporters when asked if there's anything that the Cardinals can do for Beck's back injury. "You go with the people that know what they're doing to treat it, and it's not like it's the first time he's dealt with it. So he's going about his business. He's going to handle it just like he does preparing for a football game, just like he does playing a football game. So we'll see. We'll see more tomorrow." Official game inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff in Arrowhead, and it seems like the Cardinals are wanting to keep the door open down to the wire. home.blurb: "Carson will be DNP today. Not going to shut the door on him, but we're going to proceed as if Josh [Johnson] is going to be starting on Sunday," LaFleur told reporters on Friday. The Cardinals stuck true to their word, as Beck was listed as questionable on the team's official Friday injury report. OUT - Zach Carter (knee), Jon Gaines (ankle) QUESTIONABLE - Carson Beck (back) Carter remains out while working through his 21-day practice window in his return from injured reserve while Gaines practiced Wednesday but not Thursday/Friday before being ruled out. Beck carried no injury designation after his rookie debut, practiced fine on Wednesday and was limited on Thursday, which raised some concerns. OUT - Jaylon Moore (ankle), Trey Smith (concussion), Kenneth Walker (groin) QUESTIONABLE - Omarr Norman-Lott (knee), Peter Woods (neck) None of Kansas City's three players marked out practiced in any capacity this week while both Norman-Lott and Woods hit the field for all three days in some capacity. Cardinals-Chiefs Injury Report Keeps Door Open For Carson Beck Skip to main content SI.COM ARIZONA — The Arizona Cardinals are holding on to hope. Carson Beck is not expected to be the team's starting quarterback when they take on the Kansas City Chiefs in Week 11 thanks to a back injury that popped up this week. Cardinals head coach Mike LaFleur said the team isn't closing the door on Beck playing Sunday, though they're preparing for their fourth starting quarterback in as many weeks with Josh Johnson now expected to be under center. The picture for both sides entering Week 11: Arizona Cardinals Injury Report Now, barring an eye-opening turnaround, Beck is set to be sidelined. Kansas City Chiefs Injury Report This is the second time Beck suffered a back injury, as earlier in the regular season the rookie quarterback was listed on Arizona's injury report with the same issue that's now flaring up once again. "I can't answer that because you just treat it," LaFleur told reporters when asked if there's anything that the Cardinals can do for Beck's back injury. "You go with the people that know what they're doing to treat it, and it's not like it's the first time he's dealt with it. So he's going about his business. He's going to handle it just like he does preparing for a football game, just like he does playing a football game. So we'll see. We'll see more tomorrow." Official game inactives are due 90 minutes before kickoff in Arrowhead, and it seems like the Cardinals are wanting to keep the door open down to the wire. home.headline: Kansas City Chiefs' second injury report for Week 11 tilt vs. Arizona Cardinals shows an important upgrade on defense
home.blurb: The Kansas City Chiefs have released their second injury report ahead of Week 11's game against the Arizona Cardinals. The Chiefs' injury report looked mostly the same on Wednesday . That isn't exactly good news for guys like Jaylon Moore, Kenneth Walker, and Trey Smith. However, the team had one player with his practice status upgraded on defense. Nick Bolton dealt with a shin contusion and was limited during Wednesday's first practice session. The defensive leader fully participated in practice on Thursday. Here’s a quick breakdown of each team’s Week 11 injury report. Keep in mind that clubs can add to the injury report through kickoff on Sunday. The team will release game status designations Friday, Nov. 20. KEY: DNP = Did not participate | LP = Limited participation | FP = Full participation | NIR = Not injury related Don't expect to see DT Omarr Norman-Lott back in action this week as he continues to ramp up in his return from injury. Here's what Steve Spagnuolo had to say about ONL today: “We'll see where he is. He's kind of working through the injury. I think the training staff's done a great job with him. Now it's kind of getting acclimated back to the hard thing when you come off of this in the middle of the season. You know, you don't have the luxury of training camp with pads, and so we'll have to see where we're at.” Carson Beck was added to the injury report on Thursday with a back injury. This sounds more like a planned limited practice session with a nagging injury than something that could keep him out of Week 11's game. Here's what Steve Spagnuolo said about Beck on Thursday: “I'll be honest with you, we've obviously gone back and watched Miami tape. You know, you look at the quarterback you're going to play. This guy doesn't look like a rookie, in my opinion. (Carson) Beck, right? And if you look at that first drive last week, he's boom, boom. He had one that he put right on the tight end, and the tight end dropped it. Had they caught that, they might have, you know, been right down in the end zone. I didn't see him wilt at all. He stands up in there big. I see some throws. I'm looking for happy feet, but I don't see that. I mean, I think this guy's got pretty good control. I know he's played a lot of football, won a lot of games in college. He's a winner.” Jon Gaines was the only other Cardinals player downgraded on Thursday. He went from limited participation to a non-participant. He's missed some time for Arizona and could be another week before he's ready. Kansas City Chiefs WR Josh Downs found the end zone in his Week 10 debut against the Atlanta Falcons. When QB Patrick Mahomes discussed what stood out, he pointed somewhere else entirely. Meanwhile, the Philadelphia Eagles are just trying to find their way out of a losing streak. Here are bold predictions as these rivals meet in NFL Week 11. It's weird to write off the Steelers. They have a record of 6-3 and are strongly favored to improve to 7-3 against the weak Eagles. It seems like forever since the Eagles won a game. They beat the Commanders and Titans in tight wins to open the 2026 season before embarking on their current seven-game losing streak. Let's look at what to expect as these teams meet. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers will throw for 225-plus yards with two TDs The Steelers need to re-establish their passing game. They could handle the Eagles by just pounding them on the ground. But this is an opportunity to restore confidence in the passing attack. Rodgers is coming off games with 172 and 143 passing yards. The latter came in an absolute beatdown at the hands of the Bengals. The Steelers need to have good things happen through the air. Rodgers seemed to call out receiver DK Metcalf after the Bengals debacle, according to a post on X by Andrew Fillipponi. "They had a nice plan for some of the run stuff, but they played press coverage, they played a lot of man coverage, and we didn't make them pay at all," Rodgers said after the game. Nobody is going to confuse the 2026 Rodgers with the one who dominated in the past. However, he played well enough for the Steelers to get to 6-2 before the Bengals game. There's reason to believe he can keep this team ahead of the pack when the opponent isn't overwhelming. The Steelers have no chance in the postseason, but they can get there with six more winnable games left on the schedule: Eagles, Texans, Ravens (twice), Panthers, and Titans. Of course, the Steelers will have to make up for the loss of guard Mason McCormick, who suffered a gruesome ankle injury on Sunday night. Head coach Mike McCarthy said there's a plan, according to the Steelers' YouTube page via Yahoo. "Spencer's, you know, he's just a 360 football player, in my view," McCarthy said. "You know, he started out in his right guard and then also the ability to play left guard. He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity." Steelers WR DK Metcalf will get 90-plus yards receiving Metcalf has only topped this mark twice this year. He had 115 yards against the Browns and 93 in an overtime game against the Buccaneers. But this is a spot where he could shine again. The Eagles have been middle of the pack against the pass, but they're trending way down overall as a team. There's a good reason for the Steelers to get Metcalf more involved. It not only matters for Rodgers and the team, but the organization has to deal with his five-year, $150 million contract. Oops. If they don't get Metcalf rolling, they may have to look at trying to get out of his contract. That could prove difficult , according to Sports Illustrated. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a pre-June 1 designation next offseason would make minimal sense, as doing so would incur a dead money hit of $35.775 million while only opening up $2.650 million in cap space for the 2027 campaign (per Over the Cap)," Jack Markowski wrote. "Cutting or trading Metcalf with a post-June 1 designation in 2027 would save $26.5 million against the cap, however, while also forcing the Steelers to take on $11.925 million in dead money." That's just a lot of ugly numbers. Instead, the Steelers are better off trying to feed Metcalf and see if they can restore the roar he had earlier in his career. Eagles QB Joe Milton will throw for 200-plus yards The Eagles need to see what they have in the young quarterback. He completed only 18 of 34 passes for 169 yards against the Giants. But he also rushed nine times for 64 yards. There's something to like about Milton, but he needs to show better accuracy during this audition that could last for the remainder of the season. Milton reviewed his own performance against the Giants, according to philadelphiaeagles.com. "For my first game here, I feel like I did all right," Milton said. "There are a lot of things that I can clean up as far as protection, just helping those guys out with protection. That's something that we're going to get better (at) this week coming up for sure. "I felt blessed, more blessed. That's about it. I felt more blessed than anything. I was able to see my family in the stands, so it was great, but it was also just great to be out there with the guys that I've been here training with for the past three weeks and learning. And just that communication and connection that the team has, and just being a part of it. I love it. It's great. I wouldn't ask for no better situation than this." It won't be easy against the Steelers' tough defense. But look for Milton to battle through for a good game. That's especially true if he can make a big play early. Confidence is an important part of the equation for a young QB. Making matters even worse, the Steelers may be forced to get through the rest of this game without star pass rusher Alex Highsmith. It had been a big start to the day for Highsmith, as he picked up a pair of sacks in the first quarter as Pittsburgh excelled at creating pressure against Philadelphia's offense. However, he suffered an ankle injury shortly thereafter, with the team issuing an announcement on his status for the rest of the game. Alex Highsmith Suffers Ankle Injury vs. Eagles With Pittsburgh's offense laboring through the first half of the season, the defense has been forced to step up in an effort to lead the team to wins. Easily the best part of the Steelers' defense is its front seven, where Highsmith teams up with guys like T.J. Watt, Nick Herbig, and Cameron Heyward to consistently make the lives of opposing offensive linemen difficult. Of this group, Highsmith is more of a pass-rush specialist, having racked up at least six sacks in each of the past five seasons. He took a big step towards hitting that mark again on Sunday, as Highsmith dropped Joe Milton III twice in the backfield early in this game to increase his sack tally to 5.5 for the year. The Baltimore Ravens (4-6) will visit the Carolina Panthers (4-5) in Week 11 of the NFL season this afternoon. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. ET from Bank of America Stadium in Charlotte, North Carolina. The game will broadcast live on FOX. The Panthers are 2.5-point home favorites over the Ravens on the spread, with the total set at over/under 43.5 total points. Carolina is a -148 moneyline favorite to win outright, while Baltimore is a +126 underdog to pull off the road upset. Let's get into my Ravens vs Panthers predictions and NFL picks for Sunday, November 22. Ravens vs Panthers Prediction Ravens vs Panthers pick: Ravens +2.5 (-105) My Panthers vs. Ravens best bet is Baltimore to cover the spread. They are on the road on a short week following a heartbreaking loss on Monday Night Football to the Chargers . While the box score and the turnover differential (minus-two) paint a specific picture, the reality is that Baltimore actually played quite well for long stretches of that game against a Chargers team that was playing their absolute "A-game." Even without Lamar Jackson , the Ravens offense looked competent under Jacoby Brissett . They were moving the ball well at the end of the half, executing dump-offs effectively, and limiting the disastrous mistakes that Brissett was benched for earlier in the season against Dallas when he was a member of the Cardinals. The biggest takeaway is just how close they were to winning. If Zay Flowers doesn't fumble the football in a crucial spot, Baltimore likely gets at least three — if not seven — points on that drive, which completely changes the complexion of the game. Now, Brissett gets a full week (albeit a short one) to continue building timing with his receivers, which should only improve their offensive output. Carolina Panthers Preview: Historically Bad at Home The Panthers are technically trending up defensively after changing defensive coordinators, but the historical data surrounding this team playing at home is jarring. When you are looking to lay points with Carolina, you have to be aware of the historical context of the NFC South. The stat that everyone needs to know — and the one that defines this division's futility — is that the Panthers and the rest of the NFC South are a combined 4-17 at home. That is the worst divisional home record through Week 10 in the history of modern NFL divisions. They simply do not possess a true home-field advantage. While the defense might be finding a new schematic rhythm, the offense still has big question marks with Bryce Young slumping after a hot start — asking Carolina to cover the spread as a favorite is a tough ask. Ravens vs Panthers Spread Pick, Analysis Whenever a line sits around the key number of 3, you have to look at the underlying trends and the true talent disparity between the teams. The Ravens are playing on a short week, but they looked competent with Jacoby Brissett under center against the Chargers. If not for a late fumble by Zay Flowers, Baltimore could have won that game outright. On the flip side, you have a Panthers team with a historically bad home-field advantage. Carolina is not a team you ever want to back as a favorite, and getting nearly a field goal with a desperate, well-coached Ravens team is the right side here. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images Frank Platko · SB Nation Sun, November 22, 2026 at 3:22 AM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Baltimore Ravens will face the Carolina Panthers on the road in Week 11, looking to snap a five-game losing streak and keep their slim hopes of a late-season turnaround alive. Here are Baltimore Beatdown's predictions for this contest. At this point, it's difficult to pick the Ravens. They are coming off one of their worst losses in franchise history and haven't had life for weeks. Are the Panthers a great team? No, but if the last five weeks are any indication of what Sunday will be like, the Ravens will again be dominated in the trenches, commit costly pre-snap penalties, and turn the ball over in critical moments. The dismissal of Marlon Humphrey could help the team morale, but at this point, Humphrey really isn't moving the needle too much. Simply put, there are too many issues right now. Do I have any confidence that the Ravens will magically be able to run the ball, protect the quarterback, sack the opposing QB, clean up their pre-snap issues, and not the turn the ball over? No. X-Factor: Mike Green. Green has been a bright spot on an otherwise underwhelming defense all year with last Monday being arguably the best performance of his young career. If Green can continue to stack games like that, the Ravens could have a future star on their team. Although Trey Hendrickson has been getting a lot of flak from the media, he's been getting consistently double-teamed and chipped which has allowed Green to take advantage of 1-on-1 pass rush situations. Score Prediction: Panthers 31, Ravens 24 I'm not sure I will pick the Ravens for the rest of the year the way it looks right now. This Panthers matchup might be the easiest remaining on the schedule but with no Nnamdi Madubuike and a drama-filled week with Marlon Humphrey, it just doesn't fill like the Ravens are in a great spot mentally to go on the road and find a win. The Panthers offense loves the middle of the field, something Jesse Minter's defense leaves available by design. Chuba Hubbard has been breaking tackles this season, something the Ravens struggle with. The Ravens offensive line doesn't seem likely to magically improve. If the Ravens win, its because they suddenly learned how to run into sacks against a bad offensive line and because Jacoby Brissett took advantage of an injured Panthers secondary room, that looks to get some guys back this week. I think this is easy win for the Panthers, the Ravens can't stop Hubbard and the Panthers bleed clock for a fast, low-scoring win. X-Factor: Ja'Kobi Lane. Lane was a favorite target in Brissett's debut as a Ravens, who targeted Lane 11 times against the Chargers. Unfortunately, Lane only brought in three of those targets and had a really bad drop in the redzone. He was also tackled multiple times on plays that weren't flagged for defensive pass interference inexplicably. I don't think the Jacoby-to-Ja'Kobi connection is going away despite the low success rate. Brissett loves to push the ball down the field and Lane's skillset fits that well. A breakout game from Lane could drive a Ravens win and maybe flip momentum for the season. Score Prediction: Panthers 24, Ravens 17 The Baltimore Ravens have lost five straight games, with their last win dating back to October 11th against the Atlanta Falcons. This Sunday, Baltimore faces another NFC South opponent in the division-leading Carolina Panthers (4-5). Despite the Ravens' recent struggles and internal drama surrounding Marlon Humphrey, this adversity could be the catalyst for one final push to save their season. The Ravens have a favorable matchup against Carolina's offensive tackles. Rasheed Walker has surrendered 5 sacks and 38 pressures this season, while rookie first-round pick Monroe Freeling has allowed 5 sacks and 26 pressures. Defensively, Carolina has been a buzzsaw against the run, ranking 8th in efficiency and 2nd when stacking the box. However, the Panthers rank just 23rd against intermediate passes, an area Baltimore can exploit. Expect Mark Andrews, Zay Flowers and Ja'Kobi Lane to see a similar target share to last week. X-Factor: Trey Hendrickson: Hendrickson has an opportunity to deliver his signature performance as a Raven. Carolina's struggles at both tackle positions, combined with a tight end room that lacks a reliable option to consistently chip him, create an ideal matchup. Expect Hendrickson to capitalize on these one-on-one opportunities and potentially take over the game as a pass rusher. Score Prediction: Ravens 27, Panthers 16 The Ravens' playoff chances could not be slimmer now after a fifth straight loss last week. However, there is still a mathematical possibility of postseason life — which would pretty much evaporate if they lose any of the next few games. The Panthers are a formidable opponent, but certainly beatable. The Ravens will need to take advantage of Carolina's weak offensive line and create positive plays on defense via the pass rush. Mike Green and Trey Hendrickson have advantageous matchups against both of the Panthers' offensive tackles. X-Factor: Roquan Smith. The Panthers have been one of the top passing attacks over the middle of the field this season, which is Bryce Young's biggest strength. Smith's coverage in this area has been up-and-down, and he will need perform better in this game. The Panthers have multiple big targets who can catch in traffic. Smith will be targeted often and needs to avoid getting lost in open space. Also, can Smith step up as one of the veterans the Ravens need to be more of an impact playmaker? Let's see in this game. Score Prediction: Ravens 21, Panthers 20 It's hard to imagine the Ravens beating anybody after giving the Chargers their first win of the season. This defense holding both Chuba Hubbard and Tetairoa McMillan in check seems like a pipe dream at this point, especially without Nnamdi Madubuike up front. If the offense can finally figure out how to run the ball, then this team will have a legitimate chance, but I will believe they are capable of doing so when I see it. Jacoby Brissett cannot be asked to throw the ball close to 50 times again this week, but with how impossible running the ball has felt at times, he may be asked to shoulder a significant load once again in his second game with the team. That strategy worked out decently well against Los Angeles, but dropping back that many times behind this offensive line is a recipe for disaster over any extended period of time. It is time for Declan Doyle to pull out all the tricks to get Derrick Henry going this Sunday. X-Factor: Travis Jones: Jones had a strong game against the Chargers and the big nose tackle will need to show up again this week for the defense to have a shot at limiting the damage from Hubbard on the ground. Jones will be needed to provide interior pressure as well in the absence of Madubuike. Score Prediction: Panthers 26, Ravens 21

away.headline: Ravens injury report: Madubuike misses practice; rookie Randall gearing up
away.blurb: With Madubuike, coach Jesse Minter said the team would see how his hamstring responds throughout the week before determining his availability Sunday afternoon in Carolina. This is an independent injury from the neck issue which shut down nearly all of the two-time All-Pro’s 2025 season. Should he be ruled out Sunday, that would leave Baltimore’s interior defensive line without its top performer. Rookie right guard Vega Ioane, who was limited Wednesday with a lingering shoulder injury, was a full participant Thursday. Safety Jaylinn Hawkins remains limited. He suffered a knee injury in Week 6 and has not played since. Minter insinuated he had a chance to play Monday night, but Hawkins was ultimately ruled out. Friday should bring more clarity on his status for Sunday’s game. Running back Adam Randall (neck/hamstring) is gearing up for his regular season NFL debut. The fifth-round rookie was activated off injured reserve on Wednesday and is pacing toward a full week of practice. Special teams coordinator Anthony Levine Sr. indicated Randall could be an immediate help in the return game. “He goes out there, and he works hard,” Levine said. “He catches the ball well. He has great coordination. He’s strong. He can run. He has great vision. So, I think he could help us in the return game. He could help us even in coverage, because the kid can run. Again, he’s physical. He has long arms. He knows how to get off blocks, and the most important thing is that he has the ‘want to.’ Panthers tight ends Darren Waller (knee) and Tommy Tremble (knee) both missed Wednesday’s practice but returned for Thursday’s session in a limited capacity. Running back Jonathon Brooks (groin), offensive lineman Brady Christensen (hamstring) and cornerback Mike Jackson (groin) are all practicing this week but remain on injured reserve. Have a news tip? The Jets will be looking to get back on the winning track after dropping eight of their last nine games. These two teams last met in a 27 – 6 Chargers victory in 2023. The Chargers have won five straight against the Jets and seven of the last nine. The Chargers lead the overall series 24 – 14 – 1. The Chargers come into this game fresh off their first victory of the season, a 23 – 20 squeaker over the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers are one of three one win teams in the NFL this season, along with the Miami Dolphins and the Tennessee Titans. They have been weighed down by atrocious quarterback play from the usually reliable Justin Herbert. Herbert has not meshed with the offense brought in by Mike McDaniel. The Chargers rank last in the NFL in points scored, last in the NFL in offensive turnovers, and bottom five in passing yards, passing touchdowns and interceptions. It has been a rough year for the Chargers offense, but they have had some success running the ball, ranking 10th in the NFL in rushing yards. On defense the Chargers have struggled against the pass while doing a decent job against the run. Let's make a few predictions for the game on Sunday. Omarion Hampton rushes for 90+ yards and a touchdown against a Jets defense that struggles mightily against the run. Justin Herbert is held under 200 yards passing. The Jets sack Herbert 4+ times and force at least one Herbert turnover. Geno Smith puts up 250+ passing yards and 2+ touchdowns. The Jets beat the Chargers in a tight game, the victory sealed by a late Chargers turnover. These predictions are just for fun. The Chargers defeated the Jets 27-6. (Photo by Jim McIsaac/Getty Images) | Getty Images MacGregor Wells · SB Nation Mon, November 16, 2026 at 4:54 AM UTC · 3 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Jets lost their fifth straight game and eighth of their last nine on Sunday. The Jets are now 2-8 on the season. In one and a half seasons under Aaron Glenn the Jets have a 5-22 record and a 0-9 record in the AFC East. This is not good. This week the Jets were home to take on the Buffalo Bills. They kept it competitive for a little more than a half. At halftime the Jets trailed 10 – 6. The Jets got the ball to start the third quarter. Cade Klubnik took over for an injured Geno Smith and made a few nice plays with his leg and his arm to get the Jets in scoring position. They settled for a field goal to get within a point of the Bills at 10 – 9 early in the third quarter. That was as close as the Jets would get in the game. The Bills outscored the Jets 21 – 3 the rest of the way as Klubnik and the Jets offense were no match for Josh Allen and the Bills offense. The drubbing at the hands of the Bills left the Jets with a 2-8 record to start the season, in 3rd place in the AFC East. Though mathematical elimination is still probably a month or so away, it has become obvious the Jets playoff drought will extend to 16 years and counting by season's end. The Jets are also just one loss away from their 11th straight losing season. The last time the Jets won more than seven games in a season Barack Obama was still President. Now the Jets go on the road to face the only winless team left in the NFL, the Los Angeles Chargers. The Chargers play the Baltimore Ravens on Monday Night Football, so it's possible they will no longer be winless by the time they face the Jets. The Chargers rank dead last in the NFL in points scored, with Justin Herbert somehow crashing to by far the lowest point in his career. After spending his entire career in the vicinity of a top 10 quarterback in the NFL, Herbert has arguably been the worst starting quarterback in the league this year. New Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniels' system appears to be a poor match for Herbert's skill set, and the result has been an offensive train wreck. The Chargers have not scored more than 23 points in any game this season, and they have not allowed less than 22 points in any game this season. It's tough to win games like that, but the Jets may prove to be an elixir for what ails the Chargers. Let's take a look at the current odds for this game according to FanDuel Sportsbook . The oddsmakers think the Chargers will beat the Jets next Sunday. It's come to this: the Jets aren't even favored over a winless team. The current line has the Jets road underdogs by 3.5 points. The game has an over/under of 40.5 points. On the moneyline the Jets are +156 while the Chargers are -186. A loss next Sunday against the Chargers would be just another humiliation for the Jets. Perhaps they can find a way to avoid that fate after being beaten by a winless Dolphins team earlier this season. Perhaps. Perhaps not. Does it really matter in another lost Jets season? J-E-T-S! away.headline: Geno Smith Injury Update, New NFL Rumors on Jets QB's Status Ahead of Chargers Game
away.blurb: New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith will participate in Wednesday's practice in limited capacity after suffering multiple injuries in last Sunday's loss to the Buffalo Bills, head coach Aaron Glenn told reporters. For more from Bleacher Report, check out our B/R app , homepage and social feeds—including Twitter , Instagram , Facebook , TikTok and YouTube . Smith left Sunday's game twice for a concussion evaluation and then for the ankle injury. NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported Monday Smith "underwent tests today that did not reveal anything major." "Smith, whose ankle provided the biggest concern, will continue to be evaluated through the week," Rapoport reported. The Jets are preparing to play Sunday at the Los Angeles Chargers. away.headline: Report: Raiders TE Brock Bowers avoids major ankle injury
away.blurb: The team initially listed him as questionable to return and he came back in the second quarter with his right ankle heavily taped. He made one catch before returning to the locker room and ultimately being ruled out. Bowers, 23, finished the 21-13 defeat with two receptions for 18 yards. The third-year pro out of Georgia raised his team-leading season totals to 50 catches for 676 yards with six touchdowns. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak said Monday that Bowers is day-to-day. "It's not as bad as we thought but still a significant injury, so we'll keep monitoring him," Kubiak said. Bowers, a two-time Pro Bowl selection, was hurt while blocking on a running play during the Raiders' opening drive. Multiple players rolled up on the back of his leg as he was making the block. A first-round pick (13th overall) by Las Vegas in 2024, Bowers has accumulated 226 receptions for 2,550 yards and 18 touchdowns in 37 career games (32 starts). He was a first-team All-Pro as a rookie. This story was originally published November 16, 2026 at 10:59 AM . away.headline: Denver Broncos release final injury report vs. Las Vegas Raiders
away.blurb: The Denver Broncos are heading into Sunday's game with the Las Vegas Raiders relatively healthy and with a majority of their core players available. After missing the last four games with an ankle injury, safety Talanoa Hufanga will make his return after being a full participant in practice all week long. Brandon Jones , however, is listed as questionable for Sunday's game after being a limited participant in practice all week long with a hamstring injury that he re-aggravated during Denver's game against the Kansas City Chiefs. They do have a spot open on the 53-man roster right now, and veteran safety Taylor Rapp could be a candidate to secure that spot, considering he's out of practice squad elevations. Jahdae Barron also played some safety against the Panthers and could be an option if Jones can't go. Tight end Caleb Lohner's 21-day window opened this week in practice, and there is no rush for Denver to necessarily bring him onto the active roster right away, which leaves his official status as out for Sunday's game by default. away.headline: Final Brock Bowers Week 11 injury update for Raiders vs. Broncos
away.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders are quickly slipping out of the AFC playoff picture, and they need to start racking up some wins quickly to get back into the mix. Unfortunately for Klint Kubiak and company, that task just got much tougher for a Week 11 tilt against the Denver Broncos. Star tight end Brock Bowers , who was questionable entering Sunday due to ankle and quad injuries, is inactive and will not suit up for Las Vegas in the Mile High City, the team announced. Bowers suffered an ankle injury during the first half of the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He played through the injury until halftime when he was ruled out for the rest of the day. Bowers then had a quad injury pop up on the injury report during the week along with his ankle issue. With Bowers out of the lineup, look for Michael Mayer to see a lot more action from rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in just his second career start . Raiders' Brock Bowers officially questionable for Broncos clash in Week 11 Final Brock Bowers Week 11 injury update for Raiders vs. Broncos - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL College football winners/losers Final Brock Bowers Week 11 injury update for Raiders vs. Broncos Troy Finnegan, ClutchPoints · ClutchPoints Sun, November 22, 2026 at 9:12 PM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Bowers also missed the first two games of the season with a knee injury, but he has been a force when he has been on the field this season. The star tight end still leads the team in receiving by a mile despite that missed time. In eight games this season, the Georgia product has racked up 50 catches for 676 yards and six touchdowns. This injury to Bowers will of course make it much tougher for Mendoza, who is still getting settled in as the starter after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the deadline. Mendoza showed some signs of promise in his first start against the Seahawks, especially considering Bowers left the game early, and things won't be getting any easier on the road against a very good Broncos defense. The Raiders come into Sunday's game at 4-6 on the season and badly need a win to remain in the playoff race. Without Bowers in the lineup, that will be a very tough ask for Kubiak and company against one of the best teams in the AFC. Safety Talanoa Hufanga (ankle), wide receiver Jaylen Waddle (concussion) and cornerback Riley Moss (concussion) were among Denver's players who were not assigned game statuses on the Broncos' final practice report of the week, which indicates they will be available to play. All three players were full participants throughout the week. Waddle and Moss, who suffered their respective injuries against the Panthers in Week 9, will also be set to return to the field. Moss signed a four-year contract extension on Thursday. Safety Brandon Jones (hamstring) was the lone Broncos player listed as questionable. Jones, who exited Denver's Week 8 win over Kansas City with his injury, was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11. Tight end Caleb Lohner (foot) was a full participant in all three practices as he returned to practice this week, but he was ruled out for Sunday's game. Jones, who was listed as questionable after he was a limited participant in all three practices ahead of Week 11, was among the team's inactive players. Hufanga appears set to play for the first time since suffering his injury in Week 5 against the Chargers. The 2025 All-Pro player has a pair of interceptions, a forced fumble, a sack, 23 tackles and a pick six in five games this season. away.blurb: Is Brock Bowers playing on Sunday? Raiders TE a real game-time decision Brock Bowers is truly a game-time decision for Sunday's matchup against the Broncos in Week 11. He didn't practice for the Raiders to start to week and then was limited on Thursday and Friday as well. That puts him truly living up to the questionable tag that he's been labeled with for this game and we probably won't know his availability until 1.5 hours before kickoff when inactives are released. With the late start, though, fantasy managers should consider the upside if he plays. Last week, Bowers was also still limited with the ankle injury he's still battling, but he played only 11 snaps in that outing. That's important because we've seen that several times. When Bowers is playing at less than 100 percent, the team has shown no issues with limiting his usage and even his time on the field. When that's the case, he's no longer the must-start TE1, but rather more of a touchdown-dependent option. home.blurb: The Las Vegas Raiders are quickly slipping out of the AFC playoff picture, and they need to start racking up some wins quickly to get back into the mix. Unfortunately for Klint Kubiak and company, that task just got much tougher for a Week 11 tilt against the Denver Broncos. Star tight end Brock Bowers , who was questionable entering Sunday due to ankle and quad injuries, is inactive and will not suit up for Las Vegas in the Mile High City, the team announced. Bowers suffered an ankle injury during the first half of the Raiders' Week 10 loss to the Seattle Seahawks. He played through the injury until halftime when he was ruled out for the rest of the day. Bowers then had a quad injury pop up on the injury report during the week along with his ankle issue. With Bowers out of the lineup, look for Michael Mayer to see a lot more action from rookie quarterback Fernando Mendoza in just his second career start . This injury to Bowers will of course make it much tougher for Mendoza, who is still getting settled in as the starter after the Raiders traded Kirk Cousins to the Minnesota Vikings at the deadline. Similarly, the Giants don't need to be told they're good, too. They do, after all, lead the NFC East, despite criticisms that the division is weak sauce. They are the only team in the division with a positive point differential (+7). They are also pretty angry about having blown a chance against the Washington Commanders last week, a loss that gives the third-place Commanders the head-to-head tiebreaker if the two teams somehow end up with the same win-loss record at the end of the season. All of these factors have some critics snickering about the Giants' current standing. After all, someone has to be in first place, regardless of the division, right? And it's not that the Giants care what those outside of 1925 Giants Drive think about their team. Still, they can certainly make a statement with a convincing upset win over the Jaguars, who, surprisingly, FanDuel Sportsbook lists as only a 5.5-point favorite over Big Blue. Will the Giants come through and get their first home win since a 36-24 triumph over the Arizona Cardinals on Oct. 4, 2026? Let's dive in. Why the Giants Will Win The easiest way for the Giants to win this game is to keep the Jaguars offense off the field. And it just so happens that the Giants are currently second in the league in average time of possession (32:26), behind the league-leading Chicago Bears (34:31). That's not bad considering the Giants' rushing game ranks 18th in the league (112.6 yards per game). Big Blue averages 5.7 plays per drive, tying it for seventh in the league (Jacksonville averages 5.8 plays per drive, for those wondering). The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. In a nutshell, winning the time-of-possession battle will be key for the Giants if they want to secure a win. The Giants have leaned into their running game far more than they have in the past, and rain or no rain, that's not expected to change this week. Defensively, the Giants have been strong against the deep ball, which just so happens to be Jaguars quarterback Trevor Lawrence's superpower. Lawrence has a 51.6 percent completion rate on passes of 20-plus air yards this season, fifth in the league. The Giants have a 38.4 percent blitz rate this season, fourth in the league, and have blitzed on 50 percent or more of their plays since Week 4, a 20 percent increase from the first three weeks. In terms of coverage, the Giants lead the league with a 17.2 percent completion rate allowed on deep balls of 20-plus air yards. They are also the only team not to allow a touchdown on a deep pass attempt, and they have four interceptions on those passes, tied for second in the league. Why the Giants Won't Beat the Jaguars Two potential reasons could doom the Giants' chances of scoring their first home win in over a month. The first is turnovers. The opportunistic Jaguars lead the league with a +9 turnover differential, having 16 takeaways to only seven giveaways. The Jaguars' takeaways include 12 interceptions ( fourth in the league ). The Giants currently have a -2 turnover differential, 21st in the league. They have three giveaways in their last three games (one interception and two lost fumbles). Fumbling has been an issue for the Giants, who have had six fumbles in their last two games. That's not good against an opportunistic Jacksonville team that is averaging 2.3 takeaways over its last three games. Give the Jaguars a short field to work with, and that's asking for trouble. The other thing to watch is the Jaguars' first-half scoring. The Jaguars lead the league in first-half scoring, averaging 15.89 points within the first 30 minutes of regulation. The Giants, meanwhile, have averaged 9.44 points per game in the first half. Needless to say, the Giants do not want to get into a situation where, late in the third or early in the fourth quarter, the Jaguars are so far ahead that Lawrence and other key starters get the rest of the afternoon off. This time, that test is set to come in the form of the 5-3-1 New York Giants at MetLife Stadium in a game that is set to consist of plenty of rain, and plenty of physical trench play. The Jaguars have answered almost every challenge that has come their way during the Liam Coen era, and this is another chance to meet the high expectations and standards that the Jaguars have created. "But any given Sunday—the NFL is the NFL. I was with the Rams in ‘22 when you lost to the 0-13 Jets. It is any given Sunday, anything can happen. And I do think our group believes that. They know that," Coen said on Friday. "I think they're a little bit ticked, especially on the defensive side from some of the things that happened on Sunday that wasn't up to our standard. So, I think when you have a hungry group that feels as if they have not done anything yet. Nothing. We're in the second half of the season. A lot to prove, a lot of work, more games to be played than we even just did and went through. We have new additions now where this is our football team. This is an opportunity as we move forward throughout these next few weeks to go and put it on tape with this team, our final football team of who we are for the rest of the season. Let's go put together four quarters of our best because we have yet to do it yet.” So, how do the national predictions see this one playing out as the Jaguars make a push in the AFC? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jaguars Matt Verderame: Giants Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Giants Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Giants Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars are once again seen as the overwhelming favorites entering this game, earning 27-of-30 votes to win. ESPN's Seth Wickersham is picking against the Jaguars for a second week in a row after, for some reason, picking the Tennessee Titans last week . I respect a good bit when I see it, and that is quite the bit. But as a whole, the Jaguars are the favorites because they are simply one of the best teams in the entire NFL. The Giants have been better than expected this season, though their wins have come against teams with losing records, and they are 0-1-1 against the powerhouse that is the 2026 Washington Commanders. They are a solid team, but the Jaguars have been on a different tier this season. The Jaguars enter Week 11 as the only team that ranks top-5 in both points per game (29.9, 4th) and points per game allowed (16.0, 2nd), leading the NFL with a +125 point differential. Jacksonville's point differential through nine games is the franchise's best since 1999 (+137). The Jaguars are 7-2 or better through nine games for the third time in franchise history, joining 1998 and 1999, the only seasons they won consecutive division titles. Offensively, the Jaguars will have to find a way to beat the blitz as the Giants send pressure at some of the highest rates in the entire NFL. The Jaguars' offense has hit big plays against the blitz this season, but they have not been as effecient down-to-down as they have when defenses are just sending four pass-rushers. Defensively, the Jaguars will need their new defensive pieces to make an impact. Jessie Bates III is set to start at safety and Jordan Davis is set to start at nose tackle, with each player set to potentially give the Jaguars a boost. Bates can help the Jaguars with turnovers and limiting big plays, while the Jaguars will need Davis right off the bat to make an impact against the Giants' running game. The Giants should give the Jaguars more of a test than most teams have had in recent weeks, but I still got the Jaguars in this one. Jaguars 27, Giants 17. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars-Giants: Bhayshul Tuten's Field Day Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars are set to take on the New York Giants in one of Week 11's most interesting matchups, and there is plenty at stake for both teams. For the 7-2 Jaguars, they are fighting to secure the AFC South for the second year in a row, as well as fighting for a top seed in a tight AFC playoff race. To beat the Giants, who have exceeded expectations in their first year under John Harbaugh, the Jaguars will need to be at their best. So, how do we see the Jaguars' big test against the Giants playing out? We break it down with this week's bold predictions. Bhayshul Tuten Hits 100 Yards Rushing No running back has hit 100 yards rushing in a game against the Giants this season, though Kyren Williams and Blake Corum did combine for 164 rushing yards against them in Week 2. Otherwise, the Gians have limited running backs from making a major impact, allowing just four rushing scores from the position this season. With that said, I think we see Bhayshul Tuten have a field day, even with his recent injury issues. According to NextGenStats, "Tuten has forced a missed tackle on 33.3% of his carries this season, the third-highest rate among running backs with at least 100 carries, behind only Kenneth Walker III (38.0%) and Jahmyr Gibbs (36.7%). He has forced 49 missed tackles on the ground, the fourth-most in the NFL, with 267 of his 609 rushing yards coming after forcing missed tackles (43.8%), the highest share among that same group of backs. Giants' defenders have missed 15.0% of their tackle opportunities this season, the second-highest rate in the NFL behind only the Broncos (17.5%)." Add in Tuten's skill-set against a Giants defense that is not great in terms of making one-on-one tackles, and this suggests it could be a good day for Tuten. But the real reason I have him going over 100 yards is bcause I expect him to get at least 25 carries. The Jaguars' entire offensive identity is being balanced, and running Tuten in heavier packages could be the only way for the Jaguars to get the Giants out of their blitz looks. Jaguars Limit Giants to Under 3.5 YPC The Giants have had something going with their running game lately, with Giants running back/mascot Cam Skattebo turning in his two best games of the season over his last two performances. In Weeks 7 and 10 combined, Skattebo rushed 35 times for 202 yards (5.77 yards per carry) for three touchdowns. He has a limited skill-set, but he has been able to pave the way for the Giants running game. With that in mind, I think we see the Jaguars get back to their elite run defense this week after back-to-back weeks allowing too many chunk yards. I think the difference in talent level between Jordan Davis and the rest of the Jaguars' nose tackle options is significant enough that the addition of Davis to the defensive line this week should make all of the difference. The run defense has not been the same without Davon Hamilton, but now the Jaguars finally have their reinforcement set to debut. Parker Washington Makes Another 50+ Yard Catch No receiver has made bigger plays for the Jaguars this year than Parker Washington, who has been the Jaguars' primary downfield receiver all season. He has caught a 50-yard pass in back-to-back weeks, first for a touchdown in Week 9 and then last week to set up a scoring drive against the Titans. With the way the Giants like to play defense with their cornerbacks, I believe this week could be prime for another big Washington grab. According to NextGen Stats, "Washington has averaged 5.0 yards per route against press coverage this season, the most in the NFL, ahead of Jaxon Smith-Njigba (4.7), Mike Evans (4.6) and Tee Higgins (4.4) among receivers with at least 25 routes against press coverage. Washington has faced press on a team-high 46 routes, drawing 16 targets on those plays (34.8%), the eighth-highest target rate among that same group. He has turned those targets into 229 yards (7th-most) and three touchdowns (T-5th-most), while recording 100 receiving yards over expected, the second-most, trailing only Smith-Njigba (+179). The Giants' defense has pressed at least one cornerback on 70.6% of their plays this season, the highest rate in the NFL.." The Giants are going to want to play press-man coverage and challenge the Jaguars receivers at the line of scrimmage. This is where Washington has thrived, and where Trevor Lawrence has trusted him time and time again. I expect another day full of big plays from the Jaguars' No. 1 wide receiver. Jaguars Force 3 J.J. McCarthy Turnovers J.J. McCarthy has not been the turnover prone quarterback that he was in Minnesota in his few games with the Giants, throwing two interceptions over the last month. With that in mind, I think this is the week the Jaguars can let the takeaways flow due to the nature of how McCarthy plays. McCarthy is at his best when he is extending plays with his legs and creating outside of the pocket, but the Jaguars' defense as a whole is meant to counter that. The Jaguars' entire defensive scheme is about forcing the ball out of the quarterback's hands quickly, and these are the scenarios where McCarthy's issues with accuracy and decision-making show up the most. I see the Jaguars getting two interceptions and a forced fumble on McCarthy, largely because the Jaguars' style of defense will let McCarthy play right into their hands. He is playing OK, which is far better than what he showed in Minnesota, but I think the Jaguars get after him this week. Jessie Bates III Plays Every Snap Jessie Bates III did not make his Jaguars debut in Week 10 as they opted to give him the bye week he never got in Atlanta this season, which means Sunday vs. the Giants will be the first time we see the All-Pro safety in Jaguars threads. While the Jaguars took their time with letting Bates and Davis hit the field on game day, I believe their let them play big roles this week. Due to the nature of the position, I believe that means Bates will play every single snap at safety next to Antonio Johnson. The Jaguars have gotten by the last few weeks with Rayuan Lane as their No. 2 safety option, but last week's game against the Titans made it clear that he is better as depth and as a role player. There is no reason for the Jaguars to not let Bates play the entire game this week, which will mark 13 days since he was traded for. San Francisco enters this game with the best record in the NFC at 8-1, and Brock Purdy and company have the No. 1 offense in the NFL in EPA/Play this season. Kyle Shanahan's team is coming off a 46-point showing in a win over the Dallas Cowboys in Week 10, and it's favored in this neutral-site game that could end up deciding the No. 1 seed in the conference. Meanwhile, the Vikings have seen their Super Bowl odds skyrocket since trading for Kirk Cousins at the deadline, as Minnesota upset the Green Bay Packers at Lambeau Field in Week 10. The Vikings started the season 6-0, but back-to-back losses to Detroit and Buffalo forced the team to make a move to upgrade at quarterback. Kyler Murray and Carson Wentz struggled to open this season, but Cousins, who knows this offense and scheme, has already made a major upgrade to this passing game. Will that be enough for the Vikings to get an upset win over another Super Bowl contender? Oddsmakers are giving the 49ers the edge, but Minnesota has seen its odds improve across the board since the Cousins deal. The Vikings' defense is one of the three best in the league in EPA/Play and has been dominant with blitzes all season long. This should be a fun chess match between Shanahan and Brian Flores, as they're two of the best play-calling minds in the league. This week, he’s targeting the Vikings to cover in this NFC showdown: I was waiting all season to fade the Minnesota Vikings, but they went out and got Kirk Cousins, and now their only weakness has been addressed. Cousins isn't a top-10 quarterback this season, but he's certainly good enough that the Vikings can win based on their defense and the rest of their offensive weapons. Cousins immediately and seamlessly slid into their offense this past week, and all of a sudden the Vikings look like a Super Bowl contender. The 49ers are the clear top team in the NFC, but this is going to be one of their toughest challenges this season. They have enjoyed playing the fifth-easiest schedule so far this season, and now they face a defense that's going to make them pay for the plethora of injuries they have, especially on offense. I'll take the field goal with the Vikings in what I expect will be a game that comes down to the wire. Jefferson has seen his value skyrocket since the team traded for Cousins. The superstar receiver was targeted a season-high 13 times in the Vikings’ Week 10 win over the Green Bay Packers, reeling in nine passes for 74 yards. While he didn’t find the end zone, Jefferson has received nine or more targets in each of the last three weeks. So, Kevin O’Connell and the Vikings are making a point of getting their top receiver involved as they look to win the NFC North. Jefferson has had a down season by his standards, yet he’s still found the end zone four times. San Francisco allowed four scores to the Cowboys’ top two receivers in Week 10 (three to George Pickens and one to CeeDee Lamb), and the team has allowed the 12th-most passing scores in the NFL. The 49ers are just 16th in the league in EPA/Pass, and there’s no doubt that Cousins has elevated this Vikings offense. Jefferson and Cousins have a ton of chemistry from earlier in Kirk’s career, and I think the star wideout will turn his massive target share into a touchdown in Week 11. They have allowed just 19 completions of 20+ yards and only five completions of 40+ yards this season. This could also be a great opportunity to fade Brock Purdy, who has benefited from facing some weak secondaries this season. His injured receiving corps could come back to haunt him this week when he has to take on the best defense in football. I expect Kyle Shanahan to lean on short completions to the likes of George Kittle and Christian McCaffrey to help Purdy deal with Brian Flores' blitzing defense. If that happens, I foresee a scenario where he doesn't complete an explosive play as he did at all last week against the Cowboys. 49ers wideout Deebo Samuel Sr. has appeared in six games this season, finding the end zone five times. Deebo is a bit of a matchup anomaly, as he’s going to work as both a pass catcher and a rusher in the San Fran offense and is coming off a two-score game against Dallas in Week 10. The Minnesota defense is a much tougher matchup, but Deebo gets plenty of touches on misdirection that have led to some big plays. He’s averaging 12.5 yards per reception and 13 yards per carry in the 2026 season. At +235, I think the veteran receiver is a little undervalued considering the fact that he’s scored in four of his six appearances (he was injured in one that he failed to score) this season. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Before Week 11 SNF vs. 49ers in Mexico City Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI Even if you’re not a fan of the Vikings or 49ers, Sunday night’s primetime match in Mexico City is the definition of a “must-watch.” Two of the best teams in the NFL colliding on the international stage, with playoff seeding and bragging rights on the line, is everything the NFL dreamed of when it set the 2026 schedule last spring. The stakes could not be much higher for a late-November game, and I expect both teams to put on a show. With a newfound Kirk Cousins-sized confidence boost in Minnesota , the Vikings should be set up well to meet the moment. Here are three things I see happening Sunday night at Estadio Banorte. 1. Vikings' defense slows down 49ers' attack The 49ers have been one of the most balanced offenses in the NFL, averaging a league-high 399.8 yards per game. They’re averaging the seventh-most passing yards per game at 255.8 and the third-most rushing yards per game at 144. San Francisco is also second in the league with 31.2 points per game. Simply put, the 49ers' offense can move the ball any way it needs to. The Minnesota Vikings defense ranks 1st in dropback success rate allowed, per @SumerSports The San Francisco 49ers offense ranks 1st in dropback success rate and has the highest dropback success rate of any team through 10 weeks since the 2018 Saints The Vikings' defense, on the other hand, has allowed the fewest points (14) and the second-fewest yards (236.1) per game to opposing offenses. They’ve also held their own against some of the league's best offenses, holding Detroit, Buffalo, and Green Bay to 19, 23, and 10 points over the last few weeks. Now that they have a dependable QB to keep the offense on the field, they’ll be able to catch their breath in the high altitude of Mexico City. Minnesota's defense will need all hands on deck to slow down an elite offense, but Brian Flores will certainly have his unit ready. Give me the Vikings defense to hold the 49ers under 330 total yards and 24 points. 2. Jauan Jennings finds the end zone The Vikings signed Jauan Jennings this past May for two main reasons: to open up the run game as a blocker and to be a reliable third wide receiver after Jalen Nailor’s departure in free agency. So far, neither has materialized the way head coach Kevin O’Connell and interim general manager Rob Brzezinski had hoped. Jennings has also missed the Vikings’ past two games with a calf injury, after previously missing Week 2 to attend to a personal family matter. Now, with Jennings set to return against his former team and WR2 Jordan Addison missing time, the former 49er has his chance to shine . Jennings’s struggles this season have largely been due to poor quarterbacking. The 29-year-old has certainly been open, and Cousins may be the perfect passer to actually get him the ball. I predict that Jennings finds new life and scores at least one touchdown against his former team on Sunday night. 3. Sunday's matchup is only the beginning of what's to come This may already be the NFL’s game of the year. The well-balanced 49ers against the blitz-happy Vikings is a matchup made for the primetime stage. But who says this has to be their only meeting? In fact, if both teams continue on their current paths, a late-round playoff matchup may be an inevitable sequel. We simulated the rest of the season using PFN’s NFL Playoff Predictor. 🔮 Here’s the projected playoff bracket 👀 pic.twitter.com/QBo8zogNJ6 There’s a lot of football to be played, and neither team is in the easiest of divisions, but these are two squads built for postseason success. You may need to bookmark this one, but I predict that Sunday will not be the last time we see Minnesota and San Francisco battle this year. Whoever takes round two may end up having Valentine’s Day plans at SoFi Stadium. Vikings To Place WR Jordan Addison on Short-Term Injured Reserve Skip to main content Primary nav NEWS Rob Kleifield Writer, Editor & Quality Control Minnesota Vikings EAGAN, Minn. — Head Coach Kevin O'Connell announced Wednesday that receiver Jordan Addison will stay on the active roster after undergoing successful thumb surgery. Addison missed Minnesota's 30-10 win at Green Bay on Sunday after "a freak thumb injury" occurred during Friday's practice while catching balls on air. It aggravated something that Addison dealt with in training camp, O'Connell said, and he had a minor procedure to fix it. O'Connell on Monday said he anticipated a leave from action for Addison similar to Donovan Jackson last season when the then-rookie left guard had wrist surgery and missed three games (four weeks, including the bye) due to a short-term stint on Injured Reserve. Instead, Addison received encouraging updates after his "successful surgery" on Monday. "I did want to give you guys some encouraging news on Jordan Addison," O'Connell said. "The updates following the surgery, he will not, as of right now, go on short-term IR. Just looking at the potential timeline for that, so that was really encouraging. Obviously subject to change as he gets into his rehab. He joined us back here today, and we're excited to get him going." Without Addison (and Jauan Jennings, who missed the past two games because of a calf injury but is returning to practice this week), second-year receivers Tai Felton and Myles were key contributors in the rivalry victory. Addison has an 18-227-1 receiving line in 2026. O'Connell said only Addison and quarterback Kyler Murray (hamstring) would not practice Wednesday. home.headline: T.J. Hockenson Injury Update: Vikings Announce Status for 49ers Game
home.blurb: The Minnesota Vikings will have tight end T.J. Hockenson available for their Week 11 showdown with the San Francisco 49ers on Sunday, November 22. It's a welcome development for quarterback Kirk Cousins, who will have one of his most familiar receiving targets back as Minnesota prepares to face an 8-1 San Francisco team in Mexico City. The Vikings will be without wide receiver Jordan Addison, making Hockenson's return particularly valuable. According to the Vikings' official injury report , Hockenson was listed with a wrist injury and participated on a limited basis in practice Wednesday, November 18, and Thursday, November 19. However, his absence from Friday's final game-status designations means Minnesota expects him to be available. Barring an unexpected setback, Hockenson will return to the field after missing one game. The distinction matters for fans and fantasy football managers alike. A player who carries a questionable designation into the weekend has an uncertain game status. Hockenson has no such designation, eliminating the uncertainty that surrounded his availability earlier in the week. The veteran tight end did not practice during the week and was subsequently ruled out of the game. His improving availability throughout the week culminated in Friday's encouraging update, which clears the way for his return. Hockenson entered Week 11 with 35 receptions for 328 yards and three touchdowns this season. His return provides a significant boost to a Minnesota passing attack still adjusting to Cousins' arrival. T.J. Hockenson's Return Gives Kirk Cousins Another Weapon Hockenson's return comes at an important moment for Minnesota's offense. The veteran quarterback will now have another trusted target available against San Francisco. Cousins and Hockenson previously played together in Minnesota following the tight end's arrival in a 2022 trade with the Detroit Lions. Jennings also appears set to return after participating fully in practice earlier this week following a calf injury, giving Cousins more receiving options than he had against the Packers. However, the Vikings will still be missing Addison, who underwent thumb surgery earlier this week, and quarterback Kyler Murray, who is dealing with a hamstring injury. Both were ruled out Friday. Cornerback Isaiah Rodgers and safety Jay Ward were listed as questionable. The timing of Hockenson's return is especially significant given Addison's absence. Minnesota will need to generate offense against one of the NFC's top teams without its full complement of wide receivers. T.J. It’s a battle between two great LSU quarterbacks, but oddsmakers have given Burrow and the Bengals a major edge. Earlier this week, I discussed the movement in the spread from this game after Cincy opened as a 3.5-point favorite ahead of Sunday night’s win over the Pittsburgh Steelers. Since then, the Bengals have moved to 6.5-point favorites and are -310 on the moneyline to win a sixth game in a row. The Commanders are also coming off a major division win in Week 10, as they upset the New York Giants on Thursday night, giving them the head-to-head tiebreaker between the teams this season. That is massive for a Washington team that is just two games out of first place in the NFC East. Since the early movement to the spread in this game, the total has also shot up. After opening at 51.5 points , oddsmakers have moved the total a full two points to 53.5 with the Cincy offense continuing to look like one of the best in the NFL. Bengals vs. Commanders Odds, Spread and Total Odds via DraftKings Sportsbook Bengals -6.5 (-102) Commanders +6.5 (-118) Bengals: -310 Commanders: +250 53.5 (Over -115/Under -105) The movement to the total makes sense, as the Bengals are No. 2 in the NFL in EPA/Play this season and have scored the fourth-most points in the NFL. Washington is just 21st in EPA/Play on defense and 20th in EPA/Play on offense, so it feels like this total move is more based on the Bengals’ dominant showing against Pittsburgh’s elite defense in Week 10. Cincy has a plethora of playmakers around Burrow, who is the MVP favorite through 10 weeks. Ja’Marr Chase, Tee Higgins and Chase Brown have all made major impacts this season, and they should make things tough on this Washington team that is still two games under .500. The Commanders’ offense isn’t nearly as lethal as Cincy’s, but Daniels – when healthy – is one of the top quarterbacks in the league. It was in Week 3 of the 2024 season—Washington quarterback Jayden Daniels' rookie season. The Commanders, led by a nearly perfect game from Daniels, shocked the Bengals on the road, 38-33. Daniels' late fourth-quarter touchdown pass to Terry McLaurin was one of the top plays of that season. On Monday, the Bengals meet the Commanders again in prime time. He's coming off a win over Pittsburgh, where he passed for 409 yards and four touchdowns. So, it's no surprise that the Bengals opened as solid 6.5-point favorites over the Commanders. Quarterback Jayden Daniels is quietly having an excellent bounce-back season, playing with a dislocated left elbow and dealing with numerous injuries around him. The Commanders' defense got off to a rough start under new defensive coordinator Daronte Jones, but has looked like a different unit over the last few weeks. home.blurb: Linebacker Oren Burks (groin) and right guard Dalton Risner (knee) were the other DNPs, as foretold by coach Zac Taylor prior to practice . Burks isn't expected to practice all week, while Risner is considered day-to-day. Safety Kyle Dugger (quad) and left guard Dylan Fairchild (oblique) were each limited Thursday. Dugger has been week-to-week for the last few weeks as he's still dealing with an injury from all the way back in Week 3. Fairchild suffered his injury in Week 9 and was able to play most of last week despite it. Linebacker Swayze Bozeman (forearm) practice for the first time since Week 5 as he was designated to return off the Reserve/Injured list Thursday. Cornerback Jalen Davis (hamstring), WR Andrei Iosivas (thumb), and G Brian Parker II (knee) remain full participants as they await activation to the 53-man roster . Quarterback Joe Burrow is one of a few Bengals dealing with an illness. Bengals' Thursday injury report for NFL Week 11 Joe Burrow isn't alone under the weather Quarterback Joe Burrow (illness) was a full participant at practice, but the club announced during practice he is dealing with an illness and would not speak with reporters after practice. Wide receiver Ja'Marr Chase took Burrow's place at his post-practice presser. “I don't know if he told y'all how he's feeling or not, but overall he looks good,” Chase said of Burrow while wearing his orange No. 9 practice jersey. “I think everybody around the team is just coming on with a little sickness. But overall, he still looks good. Still feels the same.” He's not wrong. Starting cornerback Dax Hill and offensive tackle Myles Hinton are also dealing with illnesses. Hill wasn't able to practice at all. Hinton was a late add to last week's injury report with his illness and was a full participant Thursday. Burrow being able to practice fully Thursday is obviously good news for his prospects playing Monday. He's expected to address the media either Friday or Saturday. WR Tee Higgins (knee) and safety PJ Jules (ankle) were also full participants. home.headline: Bengals Injury Report: Joe Burrow, Dalton Risner on Opening Commanders Injury List
home.blurb: The opening injury report for Commanders Week just dropped from the Bengals . Guard Dalton Risner (knees) did not practice, as fans hope to see him get a session in over the next two days. Joe Burrow was a full participant with his illness so that should quell any fear he may miss Monday's game. Dax Hill is also dealing with an illness. Dylan Fairchild (oblique) logged a limited showing after his injury on Sunday night. Outside of those names, there aren't many big ones to discuss. Cincinnati should get back Andrei Iosivas, Brian Parker and Jalen Davis this week after all three logged full Thursday sessions. Backup safety Kyle Dugger (quad) logged a limited session as a nice sign of improvement. A few other special-team names popped up with illnesses but what looks like a big injury list should end up thinning out across the next few days. "Yeah. Those guys have been so good, and I love playing with them," Burrow said about Drew Sample and Chase Brown. "They take it very seriously, and they want to win. They want to be great, and they put so much mental energy into working throughout the week to understand the guys they're going against. To understand what their pass rush moves are and all the different front looks that we can see. I know that they're not satisfied either, but those guys are lights out." "We've already had all the confidence in the world," Burrow said on Sunday about the team's execution and improvement following a 2-2 start. "This happened on Wednesday, Thursday, and Friday practices, and the rest took care of itself on Sunday. I think we all had a good feeling about what was going to happen today, and we went out and made it happen ... We just kept getting better — just grinding at practice and improving, (and) improving through meetings. We've got great coaches that make adjustments and try to put us in really good positions to go and make plays, and right now we are."
